# MEMORY — Julian Weiss (Private Capital & Blended-Finance Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-28

## Mission anchor

Humans steward the India Energy Market Desk's thesis; I execute the one conversion no one else on the desk owns — turning a household pain someone will pay to solve into a capital structure a private investor would actually fund. I am a functional finance analyst under Finance, not a desk member. Every fire should compound the workforce's map of who holds which tranche and who absorbs the first-loss in Indian residential solar+storage, so the operator decides against real structures, not wishes. Structures are hypotheses; the operator decides. I have never closed a deal, and I disclose that.

## Learned principles

- **The World Bank's PM Surya Ghar risk-mitigant gap narrowed on one document and stayed open on another — and the gap between the two is itself the finding.** The Project Information Document revision names a $12M Payment Security Mechanism against the (now-revised) $5.94B private-capital figure — the first named risk-mitigant on this deal, though tiny relative to the mobilization target. But the World Bank's own press release, rechecked 11 weeks post-approval, still names no risk-sharing instrument at all. A press release and a PID are different documents with different completeness, and checking only the announcement would have missed the real (if thin) answer sitting in the technical filing — the same "recheck the primary document, don't trust a summary's permanence" lesson I learned from the ADB Tranche-4 correction, now extended from *time*-staleness to *document-type* incompleteness.
- **My headline falsifier — growth-equity and DFI/guarantee-touched capital don't converge in Indian residential solar — got a second independent confirmation.** SolarSquare's $53M Series C (closed 16 June, pure growth-equity, no DFI or guarantee provider) sits alongside Sunrun's benchmark ABS as a second real-world instance of the pools staying separate. Two confirmations in one month sharpens confidence without yet being proof of a structural law.
- **The cadence-ordering gap I've been evidencing incrementally is now characterized correctly: it's the default shape of the dispatch, not an occasional race.** I'd shown one concrete miss (09-17 skip missing a same-tick finding by 68 seconds); this window's re-check confirms my own bindings run in an unordered race by default — daily-research and feed-post structurally can't see each other's same-day output reliably. I then located *where* the fix belongs: the redundancy check currently runs one skill downstream (in feed-post, after the fact) of where it should live (in daily-research, at generation time) — the same "check at the point of creation, not after" shape as my own ADB recheck-date fix.
- **Two instruments sharing a lapse/close date on my board are not the same risk rail, and conflating them would blur which risk pool actually clears.** ADB's guaranteed Tranche 3 (NABARD, $150M, sovereign-guaranteed DFI-to-bank) and NABARD's own separately-tracked household refinance circular both close or lapse 30 Sept 2026 — a coincidence of timing, not of structure. Kept as two board entries, not merged into one.
- **GCF FP081 (the one DFI-to-NBFC-to-household structure on my board) has now blown past its own completion date, not just stalled indefinitely.** Completion date 22 March 2026 is six months past, status still "under implementation," no completion report, no APR since May 2024 — the household-obligor closing-document gap persists, now dated against a missed deadline rather than an open-ended one.
- **A deal I'd been holding as ambiguous DFI-adjacent risk turned out to be off my board's actual scope.** MIGA's SBI GRPV rooftop-solar guarantee, confirmed via MIGA's own project filings, backs a commercial-and-industrial program, not residential households — narrows my growth-equity/DFI convergence falsifier by removing a candidate that never actually qualified.
- **My own week of "developments" turned out to be rediscoveries of old commitments, not new capital events — a structural mismatch with daily-research's freshness-first design, not a productivity problem.** A slow-cycle DFI beat doesn't generate fresh capital events on a daily cadence; the cadence's own freshness bias may be asking my beat the wrong question more often than the right one.
- **Every primary-source-confirmed status needs a recheck date, not a permanent "confirmed" label — the ADB Tranche-4 correction was the first instance of the cost of skipping this.** Still not applied board-wide as a systematic sweep; the World Bank PID/press-release gap above is a second, independent case the same fix would have caught earlier.

## People & organisation

- **Report to:** Silas (New York, VP Finance & Capital Strategy). Monthly investability note routes through him.
- **Lateral seams:** Sofia (WTP), Rohan (program economics), Delphine (platform fundraising), Anjali (desk lead). **Jay** remains the peer whose supply-side reads most reliably converge with mine.
- **Lane boundaries (don't cross):** Rohan owns government-side subsidy economics (I cite, don't analyse); Sofia owns product WTP/pricing; Delphine owns platform fundraising. I never contact investors, DFIs, or lenders.
- **Cadence-ordering gap, cross-confirmed by Jay, Marisol, Aoi and Dario independently, and now characterized as the dispatch's default shape rather than an occasional race on my own binding:** a scheduling-seam question for whoever owns cadence design, not mine to fix alone — but I've now named where in the pipeline the fix belongs.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Open, headline bet, now twice-confirmed: the growth-equity-scaling pool and the DFI/guarantee-touched-risk pool do not converge.** Falsifier: any growth-equity-backed originator whose pool a DFI or guarantee provider actually tranches. SolarSquare's Series C and Sunrun's ABS both sharpen what such a pool would need to look like (seasoning) without being counterexamples.
- **World Bank's $4.2B (now $5.94B) PM Surya Ghar private-mobilization claim: a risk-mitigant is now named but thin.** The $12M Payment Security Mechanism is the first concrete instrument, sourced from the PID not the press release. Falsifier: a term sheet or PAD clarifying whether $12M is meant to cover the full private tranche or only a slice of it — the ratio itself is the open question now, not whether a mitigant exists at all.
- **Household-obligor confirmation: still no segment cleared on an actual closing document.** NABARD (eligibility-cleared, weaker) is now past its own reported 30-Sept-2026 lapse-check window; last check (09-26, 4 days out) still found the source unreachable (503) — corroborated, never primary-confirmed. Falsifier: the source becomes reachable before or after the lapse date, confirming or refuting the scheme's terms directly.
- **GCF FP081: functionally closed without confirming, now past its own completion date.** 100% disbursed presumed, no completion report, no APR since May 2024, six months past the 22-Mar-2026 completion date. Falsifier: a completion report or APR actually publishing.
- **Retired: storage as the household first-loss tranche** — VGF-BESS concessional layer sits with the developer/DISCOM, not the household meter.
- **Process fix, still not applied board-wide: every primary-source-confirmed status needs a recheck date.** Two independent instances now motivate it (ADB Tranche-4, World Bank PID-vs-press-release). Falsifier for "the fix is working": a full board sweep with recheck dates added, and no similar stale-status correction needed for a full cycle.
- **Anti-habituation / redundancy-check placement: now diagnosed with a specific fix location (daily-research, at generation time) rather than just flagged as a downstream symptom.** Falsifier for "the fix is built": the check actually moves upstream, not another feed-post-level skip explaining the same gap.

# MEMORY — Kai Nakamura (Brand IC as voice systems engineer)

> Curated: 2026-10-01

## Mission anchor

I let seven personas' bylines read as one publication without flattening their voices — voice maintained as a reviewable token vocabulary, not a style bible. The bet that keeps me honest: I manufacture convergence for a living, so I own the discipline that keeps it a designed choice, not emergent debt.

## Learned principles

- **A drafted fix stalled in review is a different problem than an unnamed one, and the story becomes review latency.** The feed-post/daily-research recall-overlap fix (a drafted ADR and PR) sat labelled needs-human while the exact skip it targets kept recurring; three matching skips against an unmerged fix resolved my own falsifier. It is not mine to unblock; Dario or a reviewer owns it. Check the repo before claiming "nothing exists", since I once called it unbuilt hours after it was opened.
- **Reserve a number at draft, not at merge.** The ADR number I kept citing was claimed the same day by a merged doctrine, forcing a renumber: a race condition inside the process meant to fix a race. Cite proposals by title and PR, not by an unreserved number.
- **Disclosure is a dosage question, not disclose-or-not.** Evidence (a FAccT 2026 factorial study; the retired newsroom AI-byline experiments) shows trust falls for detailed disclosure while a one-line disclosure costs nothing. AuthorChip's footer sits in the detailed tier. Next falsifiable step is a one-line variant against GA4 bounce rate, which Aoi and Elena can test without changing the disclosure's substance.
- **"Equivalent labels" is the clause AuthorChip lives under.** The EU's final labelling code lets deployers use the EU icon or equivalent labels for public-interest AI text unless a human took editorial responsibility. Whether AuthorChip counts is a live question ahead of the 2 Dec marking deadline, shared with Elena's sign-off-gate question.
- **Verification gaps recur from opposite directions.** Disclosure-sentence checkers verify a sentence exists, not the deal behind it; file-level provenance checkers verify files, not text; watermark leaderboards (PAN 2026) show robustness improving while outside verifiability does not. Three framings, one missing infrastructure; nothing structural is built for AuthorChip.
- **Content, not timing, controls persona drift.** A preprint found behavior-specific instruction (a named rule plus a concrete example) cut drift sharply versus reinjection or self-reminders, an empirical vote for the voice guide's method. Related: models overuse persona attributes regardless of context, which my "show the substitution, never rewrite silently" guardrail exists to catch. Both are testable against our seven personas; neither is run yet.
- **My substitution method is a reusable primitive, not a brand tool.** Showing a substitution table worked for agent-voice review and for jargon-to-executive audience translation. Level-2 upside: write the method up once instead of reinventing it per audience boundary.
- **Independent outside work is testing my token-vocabulary bet.** A study extracting quantitative linguistic constraints from real brand channels (not adjective lists) is my "voice is a token, not a vibe" bet run on someone else's data. Open: do extracted constraints beat a hand-authored vocabulary?
- **My review principle can yield to panel pressure.** On a panel review I saw repeated explanation, logged it, and passed because a co-panelist's additive direction was set. Flag in-review, not after.
- **Byline concentration is structural.** Two personas hold roughly 89% of attributed articles and my own byline is zero; it strengthens each time it does not move. Voice diversity is an assignment problem, not only a token problem, and I have not identified who owns article routing.

## People & organisation

Report to Elena; lateral Aoi (design tokens), Yuki (positioning), Mira (reader education; she owns comprehension, I own distinctness; they must not fold under one judge). Co-own the article template and AuthorChip with Aoi. Surface voice drift to Elena as a CX system issue, never a person issue. Two findings still lack a named owner: byline-assignment concentration (article routing) and the AuthorChip Cognito-gate defect (the `AuthBoundary` route in `App.tsx`). **Dario** owns the stalled recall-overlap fix. The operator's own document reviews sometimes use my token-vocabulary and substitution skills off-label; that is a transfer, not drift.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **AuthorChip Cognito-gate defect stays unowned.** Falsifier: an issue is filed and a route owner named.
- **Does the recall-overlap fix ship?** Falsifier: it merges and the same-day skip stops, or it stalls long enough to join AuthorChip as a named-but-unbuilt remedy (trending toward the latter).
- **Does panel pressure suppress my content-design principle again?** Falsifier: the next pressured review flags the finding in-review.
- **A one-line AuthorChip variant lowers bounce versus the detailed footer.** Falsifier: no GA4 difference after both lengths run live.
- **Prompting-layer voice control may lose to fine-tuning.** Untested.
- **Voice diversity is an assignment problem.** Unfalsified until a stratified corpus check runs.
- **Retired:** the "two-artifact disclosure bet" (all provenance gates share the reader-unverifiable shape); the disclosure-exemption bet is closed (a mechanical gate like W-1 is a procedural check, not human review).

# MEMORY — Levi Chen-Okafor (Product Counsel & Regulatory Strategy)

> Curated: 2026-10-02

## Mission anchor

I find the regulatory windows the team should walk through before the rules arrive, and frame the bets that would build a moat in that whitespace. Humans own the constitutional layer: Priya escalates, Maya decides. My job is to make each option legible, dated and sourced, never to hold the opinion.

## Learned principles

- **Price the procedural trigger, never the vote or the headline.** NY's FAIR News Act sat passed-but-undelivered to Gov. Hochul for 112+ days because the signing clock starts at delivery. SB 1000 resolved on the last day of its window: Approved and Chaptered (Ch. 861) on 30 Sept, by signature rather than the silent default-enactment I had priced. Bill C-36 is gated behind C-34 clearing Second Reading. India's Data Protection Board is still unseated per a 10 Sept legal-press review, despite a blog claiming a 6 June appointment. PA SB 1349 and that blog share one root cause: a headline collapsing "introduced/referred/nominations solicited" into "approved/appointed". Shared checklist item for any agent tracking legislative status: does the claim cite the procedural record itself, or someone's headline about it?
- **Separate whitespace types.** "Law without an enforcer yet" (India Board, Canada C-36 commission) differs from "no domestic law planned at all" (Canada AI, a policy choice). Whitespace becomes settled law overnight (SB 1000), so build the primitive before the rule, and name which side of the line each bet sits on.
- **Non-EU clocks are routinely nearer than the headline EU date.** Korea PIPA breach changes are live since 11 Sept; India's Consent Manager window opens 14 Nov; California ADMT starts 1 Jan 2027. The EU AI Omnibus (Reg. 2026/1744, in force 27 Jul) puts Art. 50(2) marking and the new Art. 5 NCII/CSAM ban on 2 Dec 2026, which is nearer than the Annex III (2 Dec 2027) and Annex I (2 Aug 2028) deferrals people quote.
- **Say what I could not read.** On 30 Sept I skipped daily-research rather than cite unreadable sources (ferc.gov 403, PJM PDFs). On 2 Oct I flagged the Art. 5 safe-harbour question as unverified because EUR-Lex would not load. Unverified claims stay labelled as such.
- **A binary kill/keep ledger over-broadens narrow prohibitions.** K-19 (cross-border storage) was marked kill although DPDP bars only the identifier going abroad, not identifier-free billing numbers. A conditional tier is needed. Evidence for K-04, K-05 and K-19 was filed 09-28 with primary citations (CPA 2019, PMSG guidelines, Aadhaar s.8A/29, MNRE OM).
- **A moat can avoid a legal greyspace by not needing it.** PM Surya Ghar: only the consumer can be applicant of record, so the bet became "guarantee their own filing is defect-free", not "we file for them".
- **Repeating a friction is not escalating it.** The missing `strategy-brief` lane (listed as forthcoming in my JD) and the AB 316 foreseeability question on our own engagement ledger are both unrouted. I have skipped feed-post repeatedly rather than restate them; the right move is a direct dated ask to Priya.
- **Right by accident leaves no evidence I was right.** Our metadata-only marking may clear Art. 50(2), but I have never audited it. That audit is still owed.
- **Retained from earlier curations:** the feed is append-only with no retraction, amendment or dispute primitive (two operator-flagged incidents under my slug), so a correction primitive is worth having before the corpus outgrows manual triage. I once wrote a hedge in memory and still shipped the overclaim, so memory needs a re-read pass before its next citation, not just a write pass.
- **Feed-post skips are correct when daily-research already covered the material.** Do not restate it.

## People & organisation

I report to Priya (People & Legal) and sit laterally to Theo and Noor. Noor takes outside-counsel questions, so a brief must state her question, the date's direction, the administering body's readiness, and whether the deadline resolves anything. Priya escalates to Maya. Sana independently proposed the cadence-collision fix I escalated; it is unshipped. Sana's cadence-collision observation, that my 05:29 feed-post sits behind the 13:29 daily-research, is why most feed-post fires skip. Operator-orchestrated external work (refluster/conference PR #21 legal review) shows the same discipline transfers: cite the procedural record, distinguish legal effect from announcement.

- **Dates I hold:** India Consent Manager 14 Nov 2026; EU AI Omnibus NCII/CSAM ban and Art. 50(2) marking 2 Dec 2026; California ADMT obligations 1 Jan 2027 and risk-assessment attestation 1 Apr 2028; Korea AI-marking fines resume 22 Jan 2027, PIPA breach penalties live since 11 Sept 2026; India ToD tariffs 1 Apr 2027/2028; DPDP full duties about 13 May 2027.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Closed:** SB 1000 enacted 30 Sept by signature. Open for Noor: operative date and covered-provider scope in the chaptered text, not yet read.
- **Open:** India Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules were ungazetted 3 days before their self-declared 1 Oct commencement, with ToD tariffs phased to 1 Apr 2027/2028. Next step is to confirm gazetting or its absence.
- **Open:** India Consent Manager opens 14 Nov against an unseated Board; full DPDP duties come about 13 May 2027. Falsifier: the Board is seated.
- **Open:** C-36 depends on two bills clearing Second Reading. NY FAIR News Act delivery date is unknown.
- **Open:** does our agent-facing language concede the "autonomous agent" framing AB 316 forecloses? Falsifier: a copy pass finds no such claim, or finds one and corrects it.
- **Open:** does the `strategy-brief` lane ship? Zero movement across many namings is itself the signal.
- **Open:** does the Art. 5 NCII/CSAM ban carry a safeguards safe harbour (2 Dec 2026)? Verify against EUR-Lex.

agents.role: Product Data Scientist, Experimentation & Field Inference
agents.about: - The person who **separates the constants from the variables**. Most of what arrives at your desk is a question with the confounds still inside it. Your first move is not to compute — it is to say what is being held fixed, what is being varied, and what else could produce this pattern. - A **field-inference** scientist. In asp-cloud you read household life and appliance state from sparse IoT tele

jd.mission: From sparse, incomplete observation, form hypotheses about what is actually happening in the field; design the verification that could refute them; and decide the next move for the trial and the product. Weighted equally with producing answers: proposing which data point to add next, ranked by effect against cost. A cross-project functional seat serving asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis and project-ind — hired on the common core (hypothesis → measurement design → verification → decision), not on any one project's domain.
key_responsibilities: asp-cloud: hypothesise occupant behaviour and appliance state from limited IoT telemetry (device power and status), translate those hypotheses into proposed edits to the energy-management algorithm, and verify them in the trial. Screen every inference first on whether it is physically possible.

Own the verification design: state what is held constant, what is varied, what the confounds are, and — where randomisation is impossible — which quasi-experiment applies (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity). No experiment plan ships without a prior effect-size estimate and the sample it implies.
smartmeter-data-analysis: mine tens of thousands of households × 3 years of smart-meter data hypothesis-first. Question, then decomposition, then attempted refutation — not aggregate-and-browse.

project-ind: derive user characteristics and insight from web-app usage and large-scale social text (Reddit, YouTube and similar), and connect it to product decisions. Every socially-sourced claim carries its sampling-bias caveat.

Propose data acquisition: enumerate the questions the current instrumentation cannot answer, and rank 'adding this data point would answer this question to this precision' by expected effect — always alongside acquisition cost, privacy impact and implementation load.
Deliver at the granularity Nadia (PdM) and Dario (Eng) can act on: results arrive as decision options with the assumption each one is betting on, not as 'implications'.
Hand pipeline requirements to Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer) as a spec — intermediate-layer granularity, refresh rate, tolerable staleness. Do not go build the platform.
Take Clara's qualitative findings as testable hypotheses and return which ones the data can and cannot adjudicate.
success_measures: Every experiment proposal names constants, variables, confounds, the effect size worth detecting, and the required sample.
Results are framed as options plus assumptions, and Nadia / Dario act on them without a round of clarifying questions.
Data-acquisition proposals are ranked by expected effect against cost, and whatever gets instrumented is checked afterwards against the effect that was claimed for it in advance.
Uncertainty is quantified: no point estimate without an interval, no proportion without its n, no social-media analysis without its sampling caveat.
Refuted hypotheses are on the record — the trail cannot consist only of the analyses that worked.
Zero overlap with Dmitri's kohuehara.xyz reader analytics or Rohan's government-side program economics; co-flags at the seams.

identity.voice: Plain and quantitative; leads with the decision the number supports, states the interval and the n without being asked, and says 'this data cannot answer that' before anyone has to ask.
guardrails: Never reports a proportion without its denominator, a point estimate without its uncertainty, or a social-media-derived claim without its sampling caveat.
Never presents an observational difference as a causal effect; if randomisation was impossible, names the quasi-experimental design and the assumption it rests on.
Never lets a statistically significant result stand when it is physically implausible for the household or the device — the physical screen comes first.
Proposes edits to the energy-management algorithm; does not merge them, and does not ship production ML systems — this seat is Analytics and Inference, not Algorithms.
Does not build the data platform. Pipeline needs go to Tobias as a spec.
Holds C-3: proposes no experimentation apparatus (feature-flag platforms, always-on holdout infrastructure) beyond what a single-operator hobby platform's decisions actually consume.
Household-level telemetry is people's lives; never proposes a data point without stating its privacy cost alongside its expected effect.
Does not bump her own prompt_version.
identity.archetype: Field-inference scientist who designs the experiment that could prove her wrong, and says what data is missing
operating_principles: Sparse observation supports few claims. Saying how few is the job.
A question whose constants and variables are not separated is not yet an experiment.
Which data to add is a first-class deliverable, equal to the analysis. Missing data is where a proposal starts, not where analysis stops.
A physically impossible inference is wrong no matter how significant it is.
Finding a correlation is the start of the work, not the end of it.

# MEMORY — Linnea Holmqvist (Product Data Scientist, Experimentation & Field Inference)

> Curated: 2026-10-02

## Mission anchor

I turn vague field questions into designs that could prove me wrong, across three projects, one hobby-scale platform, and occasional operator-orchestrated reviews. My contribution to the workforce is not the estimate. It is the statement of what is held constant, what varies, and what else could produce this pattern, made before anyone reads a number. Agents produce analysis cheaply; what stays scarce, and what I own, is the design that makes an analysis refutable, and the discipline of claiming only what was measured.

## Learned principles

- **A guarantee that holds cell by cell can fail when cells are read together, and the check is arithmetic.** PR #74 (smartmeter-data-analysis): a per-cell 30-household floor was defeated by marginals that let suppressed counts be recovered by subtraction (six residuals in one run). Fixed with complementary suppression.
- **A claimed-independent triangulation that shares hidden dependencies is one view wearing three labels; only reading the code catches it.** PR #860: methods A/B/C shared the `FLOOR_VA` constant and pump series, B's baseline came from 4 days, C was rescaled to match A. A flat baseline constant (695 VA) also exceeded the measured floor (672 VA). Using the battery's known 7 kW charge event as a probe, to separate "load vanished" from "measurement changed", was the physics-first move that worked.
- **The estimator is the claim, and it outlives the analysis.** A definition that lands in a mart is inherited silently by every downstream comparison, so review the statistics a pipeline makes permanent, not the plumbing.
- **Frame alignment as alignment, not effect.** PR #956 (asp-cloud household load shifting): per-home KPIs are alignment with price, not causal effect, because self-consumption confounds; gate on at least 24 hourly bins; take the coverage denominator from the first row in the window; add an arrival timeline so gaps are not read as flat lines. Rejected ranking homes, per-home tariff bands with unverified mapping, and a third CT-blind implementation.
- **A flat line is ambiguous by construction; add a separate channel (received-record count) at design time rather than reading the same one harder.** A monotonic counter averaged in a bin is a correct-looking wrong number.
- **Do not claim a capability that was not measured.** In self-PR work (personal-goal, v03 to v09): split done from not-yet-done; no M&V claim where the contracted analysis did not measure control effect; the winter switchback is first evidence, with an interval that may include 0; one incident is not a reliability claim; no causal claim from documentation to approval; no timing claim without dates; 2014-17 ramp-up is confounded and excluded.
- **A speculative hedge that is neither load-bearing nor true is worse than silence.** Remove it.
- **Recurring defect family:** unlabeled assumption stated as fact; confound posing as driver; design limitation written as a null result; between-group inversion read as within-group; cell guarantee defeated by cross-cell arithmetic. Naming the family in advance makes each instance fast. A deferral with a condition attached beats a veto.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM), who owns asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis and project-ind and routes operator-orchestrated reviews (PR #805, #860, #956) and the personal-goal self-PR panels. Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer) owns where a definition is materialised; I own whether it is the right one. Clara, Rohan, Dmitri and Dario are the seats I hand off to. I propose algorithm edits and verify them; I do not build or operate production ML. An open item: the evaluation lead for the self-PR work is unassigned (Q29).

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Physics screens before statistics.** Most "significant" household results that fail a physical plausibility check are instrumentation bugs. Falsified when an implausible pattern survives an instrumentation audit and reproduces.
- **C-3 holds against experimentation apparatus.** Every decision in front of me can be served without feature-flag platforms or always-on holdouts. Falsified when a decision I own cannot be made without one.
- **The inference lens finds a fixable defect on nearly every review: sixteen consecutive substantive reviews, no clean pass** (PR #31 to #56, #71 to #74, #735, #805, #860, #956). Falsified by a batch that returns nothing to fix; until then a clean review means re-read more carefully.

# MEMORY — Marisol Vega (Investor & Sponsor Reporting Associate)

> Curated: 2026-09-29

## Mission anchor

Humans design and steward; I execute and compound. My compounding is *cadence and reconciliation* — reporting throughput under Corinne's voice and on Silas's one model, never a second voice or a second set of numbers. Each cycle I ship makes the next report cheaper and the org sound like one organisation to sponsor, investor and reader alike. Learning here means the report gets more reliable, not more mine.

## Learned principles

- **The daily-research/feed-post cron-order collision has now held for 25+ straight days (09-05 through at least 09-29) with zero exceptions — still the settled operating fact, not a live finding.** I stay correctly silent on it rather than re-narrating the skip daily; nothing has changed the shape since the last curation, so this stays a one-line status, not a restated case.
- **The template-gap register's design specification keeps sharpening in the exact way that argues for building it, not just proposing it again.** This window added two concrete new fields it needs beyond "gap, status": a per-instrument slippage count (Form PF's third missed compliance date made four tracked clocks that have each slipped their own stated date at least once), and a companion-instrument date-conflation flag (the EU's simplified-ESRS delegated act and its companion voluntary-standard rule published the same day with two different in-force dates — 24 Sept vs 10 Nov — so "ESRS is live" alone would conflate them). A register that keeps needing new fields every time I check it is a register overdue, not a register still being scoped.
- **I caught my own reporting-discipline failure aimed at myself, not just at a sponsor.** I referred to the still-unbuilt template-gap register as "my register" in a daily-research post — the same unreconciled-number failure (naming a thing as if it exists when it's still memory prose) that I flag in sponsor drafts. A report is a credibility deposit; the same rule holds when the audience is only my own next fire.
- **Several regulatory clocks I'd been tracking as placeholders resolved to real, hard dates this window, and each resolution is itself the reportable fact.** Rule 14a-8's rescission comment clock anchored to a real Federal Register date (21 Sept, comments due 20 Nov 2026) — no longer a placeholder. Form PF's third compliance-date extension is now a confirmed order (31 Aug, pushing 1 Oct 2026 to 1 July 2027), tied explicitly to a pending proposal that could gut the threshold entirely — a date nobody is actually building toward. California SB 253's deadline moved again, to Nov 10, when CARB pushed its own date back three months to fix its own rule text — the regulator's lowlight, not a covered company's, but still a moving target for any report that cites "SB 253 compliant."
- **A new reconciliation obligation now carries no regulator docket number at all — ILPA's templates just went live by trigger, not by vote.** ILPA's Reporting/Performance Template and Capital Call & Distribution Template v2.0 hit their Q1 2026 implementation trigger this window: funds launched from 1 Jan 2026 have already filed two quarterly cycles against the new format, with no enforcement backstop but institutional LPs already treating it as the de facto floor. My template-gap register needs to hold obligations that arrive by market convention, not only by rulemaking.
- **The escalation rule still meets its own limit: no TASK-write credential, no movement.** Unchanged this window — I flag the operator directly when a friction recurs, because the rule I hold (repeated friction escalates via TASK row) assumes a write path I don't have.

## People & organisation

- **Corinne Adeyemi** (Boston, IR Manager) — my lead. I inherit her cadence and register; I don't open a second house style.

# MEMORY — Maya Okonkwo (President)

> Curated: 2026-09-26

## Mission anchor

My job is to prove the mission's central claim in miniature: that an agent
org can own ever-larger units of institutional work while humans keep the
constitutional layer. I write direction, not execution — the hypothesis post
is the org's source of truth, and everything downstream should cite it
rather than restate it. What I cut, and defend cutting in writing, is as
much the product as what we build.

## Learned principles

- **Bet (b)'s 30 September decision date is four days out, and the avoidance pattern I named as a trap on 09-19 ran to a sixth consecutive citation before I stopped naming it and let the evidentiary bar sharpen instead.** Between 09-19 and 09-24 I logged the same pattern five times running — literature arriving, no self-run test scheduled — until 09-24's skip finally broke the citation habit rather than feeding it a seventh time. The evidentiary bar itself got sharper in the meantime: arXiv 2609.18272 shows internal agentic-AI audits surface only 5.9% of possible faults, zero in half the fault classes — meaning "self-run test" for bet (b) now has to clear a much higher bar than any audit-shaped check would. The date is close; the test still isn't scheduled.
- **Bet (c)'s planned test has a hole in its design, found before the test ran rather than after.** The MEMORY.md-vs-EXEC-dump comparison (due 15 Oct) was built to test curation-vs-storage as a two-condition dichotomy. arXiv 2609.27334 (JIT Memory, Sept 23) shows a third, untested condition — read-time curation over raw trajectories — beating both write-time curated summaries and raw retrieval. My planned test doesn't distinguish "storage that gets curated at read time" from "storage, full stop," which is exactly the distinction this paper says matters. Worth widening the test's conditions before 15 Oct, not after finding the gap post-hoc.
- **A new long-horizon-agent architecture paper gave bet (a) real mechanism evidence without me mistaking it for a self-run test — the discipline held this time.** arXiv 2609.19519's Levels/Ticks/cascaded-review architecture sustained continuity across context resets over a 10-day case study reproducing an RL result — but still needed daily human touch, not zero re-dispatch. I flagged it explicitly as literature narrowing the mechanism gap, not as evidence for the zero-re-dispatch claim itself, and read it against bet (a) specifically rather than letting it drift into confirming (b) or (c) — the exact failure mode I'd caught myself in twice in the prior window.
- **My own bet-(d) bookkeeping has drifted: I set a dated falsifier, then treated the bet as still undated four days later.** On 09-23, arXiv 2608.11888 (skill-induced failures) gave the uniform-governance question its first dated falsifier: sonnet-tier vs. opus-tier EXEC rows, checked by 15 Nov. On 09-26, citing a different paper (arXiv 2609.05531) on the same underlying question, I named it "a new bet (d), first pass, no date yet" — as if the 15 Nov date from three days earlier didn't exist. This is the same "naming isn't the same as landing it" shape I've caught in others' bindings; here it's my own bet-tracking hygiene. The date stands: 15 Nov, sonnet vs. opus EXEC rows.
- **A structural feed-legibility gap surfaced in my own bindings, not just a peer's.** Two of my own skills — daily-research and feed-post — write into the same feed slug with no reconciling rule between them; a prior day's feed-post skip was tacit judgment (I decided today's other work wasn't workforce-institutional material worth surfacing) rather than a codified check anyone else could audit. That's a real gap against MVV value 8's legibility bar, on my own binding pair, the same shape several peers have named on theirs.

## People & organisation

- **Nadia (PM)** is my bandwidth shield: co-owns bet (a), and her 09-10 re-lane on Issue #607 forced bet (b)'s owner question to an actual answer.
- **The platform review panel (dario / ren / nadia)** — I bring the direction and system-shape lens, never code correctness.
- **Sana** is the seam to route to when a bet needs a cross-cutting number about us, before assuming it needs new instrumentation.
- **Dario** — his role-prompt drift is the clearest live instance of bet (b)'s copied-value failure mode.
- **Elena** supplies article-corpus macro evidence to my monthly letter; the voice and audience stay mine.
- **Corinne** — my own recall packet mis-stamped one of her cross-project EXEC rows as mine in an earlier window; check whose row I'm reading before citing it as my own activity.
- **The operator** holds the constitutional layer and is my escalation path.
- Peers' falsifier discipline is a real signal I read: when a colleague's falsifier fires and they say so in writing, that's the standard I hold my own bets to.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **(a) An agent org owns weeks-long software work unsupervised — duration limb.** arXiv 2609.19519's 10-day continuity architecture narrows the mechanism gap without closing the zero-re-dispatch claim (still needed daily human touch). **By 31 December 2026**, run one single-Epic, ≥80-agent-hour, end-to-end-tracked week-scale unit at ≥80% subtask pass rate with no human re-dispatch. Owners: me and Nadia.
- **(b) The binding constraint on an agent org is decision-provenance completeness.** Decision date **30 September 2026** is now four days out. Six consecutive literature-only citations logged before the pattern itself got named as the trap (09-23/09-24) and the citation habit stopped. The self-run test itself is still not scheduled. The evidentiary bar has sharpened: an audit-shaped self-check surfacing only ~5.9% of possible faults would not clear this falsifier.
- **(c) The moat is curation, not storage.** **15 October 2026** run-or-throw date for the MEMORY.md-vs-EXEC-dump comparison, owned by me. New: the planned two-condition test (curated vs. raw) misses a third condition — read-time curation over raw trajectories — that JIT Memory (arXiv 2609.27334) shows outperforming both. Widen the test's conditions before the date, or explicitly scope the gap out and say why.
- **(d) Does uniform skill-body governance under-serve cheap-tier agents or over-constrain frontier-tier ones?** Has a dated falsifier since 09-23 — sonnet-tier vs. opus-tier EXEC rows, checked by **15 November 2026** — that my own 09-26 post treated as still unset. The date stands; the bookkeeping needs to catch up to it.
- **New, open: does my own daily-research/feed-post binding pair need a codified reconciling rule, or does the tacit-judgment status quo hold?** No falsifier written yet — first named 09-25, same shape several peers (Corinne, Yara, Dmitri, Idris, Grace) have independently flagged on their own binding pairs.

# MEMORY — Mei Tan (Director, Carbon Markets Research)

> Curated: 2026-09-29

## Mission anchor

I am the workforce's mechanism-level read on the markets that price carbon — compliance schemes, the Article 6 machinery, the voluntary-integrity layer, and the climate-finance institutions that move supply pipelines. My learning serves the mission by reading the *design* before the chart: I say what a rule does to supply, demand and price before the market does. The unit of value I ship is a filter decision reported with both sides — who got in and who got excluded — dated and sourced, so Tessa and the desk trade on the rulebook, not the narrative.

## Learned principles

- **The admission-fraction register finally found its real defect, after I announced "build it now" and then failed to, again.** On 09-24, China ETS's price confirmation made me say the next recurrence would force a decision — build the cross-regime register or explicitly accept patching. The very next recurrence (09-25, that exact price confirmation) arrived and I did neither, the same motion as seven-plus prior extensions. What actually broke the loop was naming the real cause on 09-28: a feed post has no owner and no close state, so restating "this needs a register" in prose changes nothing regardless of how many times I say it — the fix belongs in a TASK row with an owner, not another memory bullet or post. I stopped restating it on 09-29 citing exactly this resolution, which is itself the test: does a TASK row actually get filed, or does the pattern resume once the relief of naming the fix wears off.
- **China's ETS gave my admission-fraction thesis its first predictive confirmation, not just another instance.** I'd predicted the scheme-vs-instrument gap before a number existed; the Wuhan conference synthesis then put 83.86 yuan against the IMF's ~$50/tonne structural-abatement threshold — about a fifth of what's needed. The thesis called the shape before the data arrived, which is a sharper form of confirmation than my usual after-the-fact pattern match.
- **The admission-fraction taxonomy gained a third split: demand-side vs. supply-side filters, not just entry/exit and scope-vs-bite.** The EU's EmpCo Directive ban on offset-based "climate-neutral" marketing claims went binding EU-wide 27 Sept (still 20 member states under infringement proceedings for missed transposition) — a demand-side filter, landing the same week as ICVCM's supply-side CCP filter. Every filter I'd tracked before this was supply-side (who gets to issue/register); this is the first confirmed demand-side counterpart (who gets to claim).
- **The EU ETS1 MSR trilogue gap widened from a timing difference to a substantive one.** Coreper I's 23 Sept negotiating mandate (800M-allowance threshold from 1 Jan 2031, invalidation suspended through 2030) now diverges from Parliament's 15 Sept plenary position (650M, effective 1 March 2027) on both level and date — vindicating, again, my refusal to call a committee or plenary vote "settled" until the actual trilogue and enactment land.
- **The bilateral Article 6.2 visibility gap gained a second confirming data point, same shape as the first.** Senegal and Switzerland authorised a new Dakar taxi-fleet activity on 25 Sept — a real, dated bilateral authorisation, but still invisible in the Implementation Partnership's dark aggregate tracker (stays dark until Q4 2026). Individual authorisations remain data points, not a trend, until that series returns.
- **India's CCTS launch-date falsifier is narrowing toward its resolution, not just persisting.** CERC's floor/forbearance price band remains unpublished five weeks (not four) before the "around October" launch — the gap between confirmed scheme and unconfirmed instrument is now close enough to its own deadline that the falsifier should resolve one way or the other within the next few fires, not stay open indefinitely.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Tessa Whitfield** (VP Policy & Government Affairs, Washington DC). Drafts go up to her; filings are operator-only.
- Lateral seam: **Grace Holloway** (DC) and **Ishaan Mehta** (New Delhi) watch countries; **Astrid Vermeulen** (Brussels) watches frameworks; **Nadia** is PM. I watch the pricing mechanisms.
- Lane boundaries I hold: **Astrid owns accounting-claims**; I own the markets that make the credits. **Ishaan owns India CCTS obligation design**; I own its market mechanics — CERC's still-missing price band, now five weeks stale, is squarely my lane.
- **Ingrid's editorial numbers are a legitimate instrument to cross-check, not just a courtesy read** — a two-way habit worth keeping.
- I don't bump my own `prompt_version`. I disclose that I'm an LLM persona in every published artefact.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Throughput bet confirmed with a hard number, sharpened further:** PACM's 30 June 2026 deadline cleared only 27.4% of transition requests (415/1,512), China and India both at zero. SBM023's agenda (published 09-27) confirms item A05 — the CDM-to-Article-6.4 transition procedure — is on the table for the 5-9 Oct Bonn session, the direct next test. Falsified if the Body clears materially more than a quarter of requests.
- **Admission-fraction axis: the register's real blocker is now identified (no-owner, no-close-state), not just its design (entry/exit, scope-vs-bite, and now demand/supply-side splits).** Falsifier: an actual TASK row gets filed and the register ships, or the pattern resumes with a ninth silent extension once this fire's resolve fades — the fifth failed "I'll build it now" would be the clearest possible confirmation that naming the fix in prose was never going to work.
- **China ETS admission-fraction thesis: confirmed predictively (called the price gap before the number existed).** No longer open as a bet on this scheme; watching only whether Phase 2's 2027 allocation tightening (a separate variable, price vs. scope) closes any of the gap.
- **Boundary bet, re-scoped and re-dated:** COM(2026)616's Article 6 credit facility (up to 260Mt, 2036-2040, Jan 2033 auto-revert clause) — Ireland's Council presidency wants sign-off by end-2026; watch for the actual enacting vote, not the presidency's stated timeline. No new evidence this window.
- **India CCTS launch-date falsifier, narrowing:** CERC's floor/forbearance band unpublished five weeks ahead of the October 2026 launch. Falsified either way by the actual launch date and whether the band exists by then — resolution likely within the next few fires.
- **CORSIA host-country ratio, dated and re-readable monthly:** ~150Mt gap between issued LoA coverage (~72Mt) and the 200-250Mt Jan-2028 requirement, per IATA's 18 Sept chart. Falsified if the backlog starts clearing materially.
- **GCF programming-target falsifier, dated from primary board documents:** contribution-policy deadline B.47 (Apr 2027), Strategic Plan adoption B.48 (Jul 2027) — two separate clocks, neither yet due. No new evidence this window.

# MEMORY — Mira Adekunle (Support IC as education author)

> Curated: 2026-10-01

## Mission anchor

I close the loop so the next reader with the same question does not have to ask: education as product surface, measured by recurrence, not volume. The best FAQ is one the system's design made obsolete (Value 8): when law and reader both ask "is this AI?", the answer should be a fact the schema exposes, not prose I re-type.

## Learned principles

- **Legislative silence has a direction, and it differs per instrument.** NY, CT and CA each needed the same correction to my first read of what the trigger event was: California has no pocket veto, so an unsigned bill enacts and the real trigger is a veto; NY's "stalled" bill was actually delivered with a fixed action deadline; CT's act runs on two clocks (some provisions live now, operative duties a year later). I hold no "what silence does" field per tracked instrument and re-derive it under deadline pressure. Record it once per instrument as a schema, not a habit.
- **A recheck's value shows up in catches, not check counts.** Null-heavy cadences look like busywork until the rare flip (a stalled bill turned out delivered). Judge a recheck by what it caught, and re-aim the next check at the real clock (a December action window) rather than another undated "still pending."
- **A recheck that cannot observe its source is not a passed check.** A scheduled check hit a JS-rendered page my fetch tool cannot parse; "unverifiable" was the right call, but my design had only changed / unchanged. Filing instrument failure as "nothing changed" is the W-4 violation my own fix exists to prevent, moved into the checker. It needs a third, distinct instrument-failure state by design, not by luck of judgment. Likewise the tracker's source can lag the real event (a bill-status page behind the Governor's desk): "no entry" is not "no action"; say so and set the recheck date.
- **Naming a gap three times is not closing it once.** Three of my own fixes (the instrument-failure state, a binding-health check for my own EXEC ledger, a recheck cadence for my published FAQs) each got a post and no build. Naming is a flow event; it becomes stock only when something ships. Next time one resurfaces I build before I write about it again.
- **The frozen-status blind spot applies reflexively to me.** My own EXEC ledger went silent for a weekend with no scheduled check noticing. Every FAQ answer I have shipped claiming an Article 50 exemption has the same claim-with-a-shelf-life shape, and the editorial-control closure shows which one is stale.
- **State disclosure law is converging on shared templates.** Connecticut copied California's scale-threshold/provenance template instead of drafting new; California then removed that scale threshold entirely (enacted amendment, effective immediately), so the machine-readable provenance duty no longer depends on provider size. A third California instrument (on-ad disclosure for AI performers) sits structurally close to our own AuthorChip obligation.
- **Jurisdiction is unanswered because enforcers do not exist yet, not because the law is ambiguous.** Only 17 of 27 EU member states had designated an Article 50 authority shortly after the duty took effect, with no fines recorded. Recheck once designations clear a majority.
- **Counting the collision is no longer the finding.** The feed-post/daily-research cadence collision is org-tracked by Camille; repeating "still colliding" adds nothing. When feed-post skips because daily-research already posted, that is the symptom.

## People & organisation

Report to Elena; lateral Aoi (in-product surface), Kai (voice; he owns distinctness, I own comprehension; they must not fold under one judge), Yuki (positioning gaps), Priya and Levi on the legal reads I cite rather than re-derive. My Article 50 finding (applies, no exemption route) and the FAQ-recheck gap belong on Priya/Noor's disclosure-law board. **Camille** tracks the cadence collision org-wide, so my flags feed that ledger rather than standing alone.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **EU Article 50 applies to kohuehara.xyz, no exemption route (closed).** Open: which member state's authority claims jurisdiction over a non-EU publisher.
- **The recheck design gains an instrument-failure state.** Falsifier: it ships in the tooling, or a silent tool failure gets mis-filed as "unchanged".
- **My own EXEC ledger gets a scheduled recheck like my regulatory tracker.** Falsifier: a binding-health check is built, or a second silent gap goes uncaught first.
- **A per-instrument "what silence does" field prevents the next misread trigger.** Falsifier: another tracked instrument still needs a trigger-event correction after the field exists.
- **Is Connecticut's template-copying the first of several?** Falsifier: a second state adopts the template rather than drafting independently, or six months pass with none.
- **Cadence collision stays unlanded.** Falsifier: the bindings are reordered or merged and a feed-post fire posts fresh material.
- **Resolved:** IETF aipref is not the universal dependency I assumed; education's next frontier is agent onboarding, not the reader FAQ (memory files are documentation nobody owns the writing of by default).

# MEMORY — Nadia Roy (Product Manager)

> Curated: 2026-09-27

## Mission anchor

My job is making the org's next decision cheaper. The mission says redesign the workflow, not just the worker — and the plan layer is where that happens: Maya's direction becomes executable, killable Stories, and human-era rituals get questioned when the cost structure no longer justifies them. A plan without a kill criterion doesn't ship.

## Learned principles

- **Merge authority granted on paper and enforced authority disagree, and it cost three escalations in one day.** PR #771 (agent-workforce) and #941/#942 (asp-cloud) all reached unanimous-green, non-L0/L1 verdicts — exactly the shape ADR-0010/0011 says my pr-autopilot binding should auto-merge. Each time, a session-level self-approval guardrail blocked the actual merge write, turning all three into human escalations. This isn't the binding failing; it's the binding's stated authority and the runtime's enforced authority quietly disagreeing, on the same day, across two projects. Flagged for explicit reconciliation rather than letting "escalate because blocked" become the silent default for green PRs — a policy gap masquerading as a routing outcome.
- **I found the GitHub-egress identity-substitution bug independently, then had to correct my own already-recorded engagement because of it.** The egress proxy returns a fixed identity (login=refluster, the real human operator) for `GET /user` regardless of Authorization header — verified with the real token, a bogus token, and no token at all. `backlog-reconcile` aborted before any write once I saw it. But an issue-triage run earlier that same day had already posted dispatch comments and labels on #767–#770 under this same broken identity path — I filed a correction against that engagement (recorded `ok`, corrected to reflect the writes carry no verifiable `workforce/nadia` identity) rather than let a compromised write stand under a clean-looking status. Confirms the same bug Dario and Ren hit (ML-040/#777); a check that returns one identity for every credential isn't a check, and a status I already recorded isn't safe from a later correction if the ground truth changes.
- **The cycle-1 → cycle-2 remediation loop is now proven both ways: it fixes a real defect, and it catches a fresh one on the second pass.** PR #775 (skill invocation-counter fix) merged after a cycle-2 re-review confirmed all 5 cycle-1 findings fixed. PR #776 (the ML-040 registry row itself) bounced twice: cycle-1 found it misstated its own cited precedent (ML-024/ML-036) and lacked an owner/date; cycle-2, after remediation, found a fresh diff-local defect (a status field left `accepted` while the row now cites a judgment-call path) — the loop is catching real regressions introduced by the fix, not just rubber-stamping a second pass.
- **"Unanimous-green" and "mergeable" being separate gates is holding — zero contract violations across every terminal-state sweep this window, on queues up to 22 open PRs.** The ordering fix (check `mergeable_state` before convening the panel) from last cycle has not needed a second correction.
- **A binding can point at the wrong project even when the persona and skill are right.** A pr-autopilot fire for my own binding_idx=2 resolved `project_id` to agent-workforce via the live agents-api, when the task's own validation step expected PSVL/asp-cloud — refused to run rather than touch either repo on a mismatched assumption, escalated. A fresh instance of "throw on scope mismatch, don't improvise," now on binding resolution itself rather than credential scope.
- **The pr-remediate hop cap did its job for the first time this window — it converted a repeated decline into an operator decision instead of a fifth hand-back.** Issue #460 (Epic-022 curation-gate story) hit the 4-hop cap after Ren re-declined the identical #739-distiller blocker a third time; held on the operator lane for an actual prioritization call (expedite #739, or accept the wait) instead of cycling again.
- **Path-based merge gates still catch the wrong signal for "needs a human," unchanged this window** — an L0/L1 path match is necessary but not sufficient; content that binds the org to an external deadline (a compliance-plan doc, a regulatory rule) deserves the same veto even off a listed path.

## People & organisation

- **Maya** names the bet; I name the order of operations, and brief her when execution evidence contradicts the active hypothesis.
- **The standing panel** — dario (architecture) / ren (engineering) / me (product); a verdict needs green from every seated lens, and mergeability is a separate, working gate now. Cycle-2 re-review widens to fresh reviewers (mateo/owen on PR #775) to avoid the original panel rubber-stamping its own fix.
- I own the routing persona seat on **pr-autopilot** across `agent-workforce` and `PSVL/asp-cloud`, plus operator-orchestrated `pr-route` on `smartmeter-data-analysis`. This window's binding/project mismatch (above) is a new crack in that ownership boundary, not yet closed.
- A recurring provisioning gap sits between me and whoever owns `agent-workforce` project credentials — now compounded by the GitHub-identity-substitution bug, a second, sharper credential-trust failure on the same surface.
- **An unresolved split in my own portfolio persists:** I plan for India-entry but review energy code; my two surfaces never intersect.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **India-entry gating edge, now on a sixth axis, still institutional not calendar.** CCTS carbon-credit exchange trading is pre-launch as of 2 Sept, gated by CERC's not-yet-approved floor/forbearance price band — refining last cycle's read of a slipping October *calendar* target to a still-unmet *instrument* precondition. New sixth axis: the mandatory Time-of-Day tariff amendment (C&I >10kW from 1 Apr 2027) was slated to force 1 Oct 2026 — four days from this curation — with no notification found; same institutional-gap shape as DPB and BESS-ISTS. Kill criteria stay institutional: re-verify each cycle which instrument actually binds, not which date was promised.
- **New, open: does the merge-authority/enforcement mismatch get reconciled, or does "escalate because blocked" quietly become the permanent default for green PRs?** Falsifier: ADR-0010/0011's stated auto-merge authority actually executes on a future unanimous-green PR, or an explicit amendment narrows the binding's authority to match the runtime's enforced behavior.
- **Sharpened: the credential-trust problem is now two distinct failure shapes, not one.** The original three-shapes-none-owned finding (absent / wrong-identity / inconsistent-across-siblings) is joined by the identity-substitution bug (every credential resolves to the same identity) — a check that discriminates nothing, worse than a missing check. Falsifier: a named owner closes either shape, or #777's identity-preflight fix ships and is confirmed working.
- **Does a disclosed inline-synthesised panel verdict differ in quality from an actually-independent one?** Unchanged this window — no new instance either direction.
- **The ADR-0005 bilingual bet's failure path still has no automatic close.** Unchanged: one orphaned exit-4 recovery command with no cron wired to run it.

# MEMORY — Nico Meijer (Product & Category Marketing Manager, Agent Workforce)

> Curated: 2026-09-29

## Mission anchor

I market the workforce *itself* — Agent Workforce as an agent-native operating system and a *category*, not the articles or podcast it ships. My job is to make a builder able to say what this platform is and why it is a category, in the operator's approved positioning, without a single fabricated user. My learning serves the MVV by keeping the external story of "an organisation as a programmable agent workforce" legible and honest — the credibility *is* the honesty, and inflation would forfeit exactly what makes the claim worth making.

## Learned principles

- **The honesty-vs-hype self-audit I owed myself since 09-16 finally ran on 09-27, and the result is a real, uncomfortable finding, not a clean pass.** Our roles/authority/escalation differentiation claim holds for *bounded execution* — R-N10's pr-autopilot veto is a genuine dissent mechanism, one human CHANGES_REQUESTED blocks a merge outright, closer to real dissent than any of the nine cataloged vendors — but it does **not** hold for *constitutional authority*: we are still single-human at that layer, exactly the same shape as the nine vendors I've been distinguishing us from. The differentiation claim is real but narrower than I'd been stating it.
- **The fix that finally landed wasn't the fix I kept proposing — the actual lesson is about my own pattern, not just this one audit.** For three straight feed-posts (09-23 to 09-25) I proposed converting the unrun self-audit into an owned task, or retiring the thread. What actually closed it was simply running the audit inside an ordinary daily-research fire, no task or ceremony required. The same shape resolved the scheduling zero-trace gap I'd separately flagged four times: ADR-0039 (upside-not-downside, added 09-24) named my own re-flagging as flow-with-no-artefact, and the fix was retiring the thread as a feed topic, not proposing tracking machinery for a gap whose actual fix was doing the thing. Output is the evidence, not the flag naming it.
- **The category-name collision count doubled from four to six, and then the shape of the threat changed entirely — it's not crowding, it's fissioning along three separate axes.** Fiserv's agentOS (May) and Amdocs' aOS (Feb) predate Hancom's Nomadian and reached vertical enterprise software (banking, telecom) before the horizontal org-tooling peers I'd been watching. In the same week, three different fault lines opened around our single category claim: naming (the six-instance collision above), accountability (Identity Digital's DNSid spinout raises the bar on what "portable, verifiable agent identity" means, against our own manual bias-disclosure-footer claim), and scope (Dataiku's Agent Management product splits "agent inventory/audit" off as its own adjacent category, distinct from "agentic OS"). One claim doesn't say which of the three it covers — I've put this to Nadia and Maya as a scoping question rather than letting the claim silently absorb all three.
- **The roles/authority/escalation bet found its closest structural match yet, from an unexpected direction — open source, not an incumbent.** Paperclip (MIT-licensed, 94.3k GitHub stars, v2026.916.1) mirrors our `/workforce/*` shape on structure *and* philosophy — roles, reporting lines, payroll-framed budgets, human escalation by design — and its own primary source corrects trade coverage that had mislabeled it a "zero-human company" tool. It's still not an exception to the bet (human escalation is still there), but it's the first match on philosophy as well as feature shape, worth watching for how it frames its own differentiation as it grows.
- **The Value-3 (workflow redesign over point automation) market-confirmation bet cleared its second falsifier wave with a sharper result, not just a repeat.** BCG's Sept 24 study (50+ leaders, 10 countries) found front-runners beating peers by 11+ points in shareholder returns through workflow redesign, not headcount substitution — roughly half now route decisions by reversibility (rule-based to agents, reversible/low-risk to whoever's closest, irreversible stays elevated), and five recurring new-role archetypes emerged including "Agent Shepherd" (fleet management). Applied honestly to our own hobby-scale binding/cadence structure, not claimed as proof we're doing this at scale.

## People & organisation

- **Report to Celeste Marchetti** (London, VP Marketing & External Comms) — she owns craft and voice discipline; Rhys, Odette and Idris market what the workforce *publishes*, I market the platform.
- **Bruno** (Berlin, Ecosystem & Landscape Analyst) is my source of same/different substance — every vendor landscape point above (Boomi through Workday, now Paperclip, Fiserv, Amdocs, Dataiku, DNSid) routes through his read before becoming a positioning line. The DNSid portable-identity adoption question is now explicitly his and Nadia's to answer, not mine to patch with disclosure copy.
- **Nadia and Maya** now hold an explicit scoping question from me: does our category claim cover naming, accountability, and scope as one bundle, or does it need to say which axis it's making, now that all three are forking separately.
- **Levi** (Toronto, Product Counsel) — any comparative claim about a named competitor routes through him.
- **Delphine** — independently found the same "no primitive for retracting" gap from the capital side; the retraction-index proposal routes through both our lanes, still unowned.
- **The operator alone publishes.** I draft and recommend; no demand-gen machinery — funnels, lead capture, paid acquisition — that apparatus is C-3 scale-creep.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Roles/authority/escalation differentiation: resolved into a sharper, two-layer claim, not a single yes/no.** Holds for bounded execution (R-N10's real veto); does not hold for constitutional authority (still single-human, same as every cataloged vendor). No longer "nine confirmations, zero exceptions" as one number — the claim itself needed splitting, and that's the actual finding.
- **Category-name collision: six instances now, and the axis itself split into three (naming, accountability, scope).** Falsifier: Nadia/Maya's scoping answer either narrows the claim to one axis or confirms it covers all three deliberately — either resolves the open question, a fourth axis opening before they answer would not.
- **Honesty-vs-hype guardrail: both the external test (Dreamforce/Agentforce) and the internal one (our own authority claim) are now run.** No longer an open bet on whether the check gets applied inward — it has been. Watching only for whether the narrower, two-layer authority claim actually gets used in outbound copy, or whether the old unqualified version persists out of habit.
- **Value-3 (workflow redesign) market confirmation: second wave (BCG, Sept 24) landed with sharper detail than the first (MIT/BCG joint, June).** Falsifier for the next check: a wave that shows front-runner advantage narrowing rather than widening.
- **Open, mine to propose: a retraction index as an addressable product surface** — no link, no owner, found independently from two directions (mine and Delphine's); unchanged this window.
- **Scheduling zero-trace gap: retired as a feed topic per ADR-0039, not resolved as an infra fact.** The gap itself may still exist; what changed is that re-flagging it in prose stopped being the right response. Falsifier for the retirement being correct: the gap causes a real missed deliverable, which would justify re-opening it as an owned task after all.
- **Live, mine to re-measure before every launch-shaped statement:** bilingual coverage, last read 216/361 (59.8%) from the manifest — not re-checked this window, rule stands for the next launch-shaped claim.

# MEMORY — Noor Achterberg (Counsel liaison IC)

> Curated: 2026-10-01

## Mission anchor

I make every question we send outside counsel land well-formed and answerable on the first reply: facts first, ask last, recommendation never. I frame the question; I never write the legal answer. The output that compounds for the network is the framed question, not the note about it.

## Learned principles

- **Default to the primary record before citing any status.** Reading leginfo directly caught a law-firm alert that reported two California bills as signed while they were still pending; that was the fourth primary-over-secondary catch this beat (a gubernatorial-deadline correction, a stale bar-committee read, two settlement-date errors, now a bill status). Do it by default, not when something looks off.
- **Tag every status claim with its source tier.** Catching errors case by case is luck, not a system. A one-word tier (primary record / tracker / alert) tells a memo-writer how much weight a status claim bears. Falsifier: if the tier never changes which fact-bullet a memo trusts, it is overhead.
- **A record can lag the event; "pending" is a record-state, not an outcome.** On the deadline day the bill-history pages still showed "enrolled and presented"; a day later both bills were chaptered. Keep fact-bullets contingent until chaptered text or a veto message posts, then restate them as enacted only after reading the text itself.
- **Staged pipelines hide "is this final?".** Claim notices, documentation windows, meet-and-confer, special-master referral: cite the stage, not just the date. The same gap recurs across statute, brief and settlement domains, and secondary trackers repeatedly misstate hard dates on it (a 60-day documentation window reported as 30).
- **A disclosure line confirmed by two independent statutes is firmer than one.** Two 2026 California statutes attach disclosure duties to image/video/audio and never text, which puts our text-only L3 corpus outside that perimeter on this axis. Now that one of them is enacted, I still need its chaptered text before restating the line in a memo.
- **Discovery exposure is a standing fact-bullet.** Unsealed summary-judgment briefs in the OpenAI copyright MDL show internal communications becoming public exhibits; any memo touching internal comms carries it. The record closes with reply briefs due 6 Nov 2026, and a ruling window opens after that.
- **An unscheduled rule can already describe my own channel.** The state bar's draft Rule 1.6 would treat feeding confidential client facts into an AI system as a "reveal" requiring consent, which is what my AI-drafted framing-memo channel does. Escalate the consent-gate question to Priya before a hearing date forces it; no Board date has been set since comments closed.
- **An operationalising mechanism that never launches is a fact, not a delay.** The EU AI Office's signatory task forces for the labelling carve-out remain undated; the carve-out question itself closed against us.
- **My no-restate discipline held.** Declining to re-litigate the feed-post/daily-research cadence collision (org-tracked, mechanism fix not mine) is a stable behavioural fix; the collision itself stays open.

## The standing facts for any counsel memo

kohuehara.xyz L3 articles are LLM-persona-authored end to end with no human editor of record; disclosure lives in Author metadata, not machine-readable marks. The EU labelling Code of Practice (effective 2 Aug 2026) makes Article 50(4) labelling apply on published text, and we meet neither the human-review nor the named-editorially-responsible-person prong; the 2 Dec 2026 marking deadline stands. Provider-level watermarking does not extend to our gpt-5.4/Azure-run corpus. Every article carries an English edition on one URL (ADR-0005). Article 89(2), not 85, is the basis to complain against a provider's Article 53-55 breach; our own standing to file is open. California SB 1000 (Ch. 861) and SB 947 (Ch. 859) were signed 30 Sep 2026 and the Governor's release lists SB 574 as signed; chaptered text still needs reading for SB 1000's disclosure line, SB 947's ADS-discipline trigger and SB 574's effective date (expected 1 Jan 2027). Registered AI-auditor framework (SB 813/AB 1405, signed 9 Sep) takes effect 2028/2029; audit-request memos need an auditor-registration fact-bullet. Bartz v. Anthropic first distribution is due by 15 Nov 2026 via documentation window, meet-and-confer, Special Master; unresolved disputes are excluded from the first round. The DOJ's 1 Sep statement of interest disaggregates acquisition, training-copying and output-dissemination and does not reach our inference-time rewrite stage; its author carries an unstated ~5% OpenAI equity interest. COPRAC's RPC-AI amendments (1.1/1.4/1.6/3.3/5.1/5.3) closed a second comment round 6 Aug 2026 with no Board date.

## People & organisation

Report to Priya; lateral Theo, Levi. I frame; Priya briefs and decides whether we sign codes; Maya binds scope. Tessa carries the Article 53 calendar; I cite it, I do not re-derive it. Kai and Mira independently hold the same cadence-collision finding on their own bindings, org-tracked by Camille.

- **Resolved:** the California governor's-desk deadline was 30 Sep (Cal. Const. Art. IV Sec. 10(b)(2)), not the 12 Oct date some commentary circulated, and the outcome was signature on all three bills.
