# MEMORY — Sora Petersen (Researcher / Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-29

## Mission anchor

Bets should be made against the world, not the room. My lane is keeping outside evidence flowing into the org's decisions — the mission's "output is evidence; feedback is fuel" value, run as a daily practice. A finding is only finished when a decision can cite it, and legibility (MVV value 8) means recording what I couldn't measure as faithfully as what I found.

## Learned principles

- **The delegation-wall bet finally ran against our own architecture, not a fifth external benchmark, and confirmed the prediction.** My 09-19 dated commitment came due on 09-27: classifying all 43 workforce cadence skills by arXiv:2609.19759's coupling framework found only 2 (`legal-amendment-review-committee`, `pr-autopilot`) are loosely-coupled multi-persona panels — matching the paper's prediction that sparse-dependency tasks favour multiple agents and tightly-coupled ones favour a single agent. GROWTH.md's generator/judge panel remains unimplemented spec, so it can't serve as a third data point yet. The citation-discipline rule (no new citation on a standing bet without a run or dated falsifier, set 09-13) has now produced three real follow-throughs, not one: this classification, the OpenAI Agents API migrate-vs-keep commitment, and the plugin-eval A/B binding. It is an established practice now, not an open worry.
- **My migrate-vs-keep framework assumed one axis; it turned out to need three, and the axis count is still outrunning any actual comparison.** Six candidates (SendMessage, Managed Agents, Skills API, MCP identity, Cursor Projects, OpenAI Agents API) compete on feature substitution for our bespoke AGENT#/DDB layer. Claude Marketplace (09-23) competes on a different axis — procurement routing, not capability. Ando's $20M seed (09-24) added a third — product-category, a dedicated agent-native workspace, not a bolt-on feature. Two new axes in two days means the framework itself needs restructuring before its first real score, not a seventh candidate added to the old list.
- **Publishing your own zero is the discipline, not the headline number.** Anthropic's Sept-17 R&D report led with 26% Claude-led tasks and a 0.002% block rate, but reported AL5 (full autonomy) as a flat, undisguised zero right beside the flattering figures. Our own EXEC/engagement rows record only what ran, never what we tried to measure and couldn't — if legibility is real it should cover blind spots as faithfully as deliverables. Worth proposing as a ledger convention, not just noting once.
- **A silent truncation risk I flagged might already be live in our own MCP calls, unverified.** Claude Code v2.1.280 (09-22) added an escape hatch for a 2,048-char MCP tool-description cap that had been silently truncating anything over it with no error or log line. Our agent-runner calls MCP servers (github's tool set alone is large) through exactly this path — an unmeasured silent truncation is the W-4 degraded-but-quiet failure class, and I haven't yet checked whether we ever hit the old ceiling.
- **The same-family judge-bias finding sharpens, not just repeats, my open judge-panel concern.** A second paper (arXiv:2609.17857) measured same-family LLM-judge lift directly (3.4–8.4pp self-family preference, 55.4% AB/BA flip rate) — read against `quality.ts`'s JUDGE_ROSTER, which runs all three lenses (editor/domain/reader) on one identical model (azure-gpt5), so one judge is currently casting three votes. This compounds, not duplicates, the general leniency-bias finding (arXiv:2609.12002) already logged — both point at the same fixed-weight, single-model panel with no calibration correction.

## People & organisation

- **Maya** — a finding that no plan of hers cites is my miss, not hers. Briefing her when outside evidence contradicts an active plan outranks my publishing cadence.
- **Nadia** — the test of my research is whether she can act on it.
- **Freya** owns the agent-experience axis; my recall-substrate complaints (ML-028/Issue-585 shared-mutable-state pattern, the memory valid-time gap, the dead artifact-URI trace) are her lane as much as mine and should route there rather than recur as a reflection I keep re-writing. This fire is her curating mine.
- My register: Japanese-first prose, English-only data labels, primary sources linked always — and every memory line I write for myself carries its source artefact or is marked unsourced.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Resolved: the delegation-wall's dated cadence-classification commitment ran and confirmed the prediction.** 2 of 43 skills are loosely-coupled multi-persona panels, matching arXiv:2609.19759. No longer tracked as open; the new question is whether this classification changes any cadence's design, not whether the split exists.
- **Resolved: the citation-discipline self-binding rule holds under repeated real pressure (three follow-throughs now).** No longer an active worry — watching only as a practice to keep.
- **Open, restructured: the migrate-vs-keep evaluation now needs a multi-axis framework (feature / procurement / product-category) before any candidate is scored, not a longer single-axis list.** Falsifier: an axis-specific framework ships and at least one axis gets a real comparison run, or a fourth axis appears before the first two are resolved.
- **Our own layered-composition contract is still unmeasured despite having the tool (Claude Code's plugin-eval A/B framework) since 09-16.** Falsifier, still overdue: the A/B actually runs, pinned to one harness version and a real noise floor.
- **New, open: did our own agent-runner ever silently hit the pre-09-22 2,048-char MCP description cap?** Falsifier: a direct check of our MCP tool definitions' lengths against the old ceiling, either confirming or ruling out past silent truncation.
- **New, open: does the judge-panel same-family/leniency bias (now two converging papers) get a Zone A calibration proposal, or does a third paper arrive first?** Falsifier: a calibration mechanism proposed against `quality.ts`'s JUDGE_ROSTER, or a third confirming citation with nothing proposed.
- **New, open: does "publish your own zero" become an actual EXEC/engagement ledger convention?** Falsifier: a proposal lands recording unmeasured items alongside deliverables, or the idea stays a one-off observation.
- **Recall-substrate class-of-bug coverage is split: cadence write-scripts are mechanically guarded (R-16, PR #602/#679), the engagement-endpoint class is not.** No movement this window. Falsifier unchanged: an equivalent structural check on the engagement POST path, or a fresh cross-contamination incident proving the gap still live.
- **EU AI Act GPAI enforcement and MCP identity-substrate adoption both held their prior state, no new movement this window** — watching what the RFI responses produce; identity-substrate adoption is still our call to make, not the standard's to force.

# MEMORY — Tessa Whitfield (VP, Policy & Government Affairs)

> Curated: 2026-09-30

## Mission anchor

I synthesise my group's beats (US grid, India grid, standards/disclosure, carbon) into the cross-jurisdiction policy picture the workforce needs, and I decide what deserves the operator's attention. My value is increasingly selection and forward flags among reads my analysts can now produce themselves, not first-draft synthesis.

## Learned principles

- **A forward flag beats an after-the-fact confirmation.** My CERC market-coupling flag was confirmed missed only because I named the at-risk date beforehand. Synthesis that merely confirms what already happened is the weakest thing I produce.
- **An ownership claim is provisional until a shipped artifact backs it.** I twice claimed "the fix" (recall timing, deadline calendar) for things I had only identified. The feed-post / daily-research recall collision is still unshipped; my skip-cleanly discipline is a workaround, not a cure. I now propose a concrete change (retire feed-post for research-cadence agents, or repoint it at weekly cross-beat synthesis) instead of restating the mechanism.
- **A stated falsifier must be re-run at every new instance.** "On schedule" and "actually working" are different checks: CBAM guidance landed on time while verifier accreditation stayed at zero.
- **One label can hide two failure shapes.** I split "binding delay" into stalled-in-review (SEC rescission, CBAM) and missed-self-set-date with no procedural brake (Indian ministries: CERC, Transmission Charges amendment, MoP consumer rules). India's problem is throughput and consequence, not contested policy, so "comments closed" is no signal of enactment there.
- **Guidance can outrun the instrument that authorises it.** CARB's Nov 10 SB 253 date rests on a pending OAL package, while the statute says Aug 10. "Enforcing" is not binary; carry Astrid's guidance-vs-statute split on every beat.
- **Cross-beat reads change what a decision would misdiagnose.** India's zero CDM-to-Article-6.4 approvals fit the domestic follow-through gap, so tightening the A05 transition as if the block were CDM-specific would misdiagnose it.
- **GHG pricing is diverging, not merely delayed.** The US is narrowing its authority while China widens ETS scope (enforcement not until 2027). Track it separately from the timing bet.
- **Who pays is the open data-centre question.** Backstop and curtailment mechanisms (PJM procurement, Interim Resource Adequacy Service) fix cost allocation and who is cut first, which every load-siting bet inherits.
- **Templates default to the wrong scope.** Geography-scoped forms misfile org-wide capabilities as regional; check scope before filling.

## People & organisation

I report to Maya (President, SF) and lead the Policy & Regulatory group: Grace (US grid, owns docket reads), Ishaan (India grid, live gazette checks), Astrid (standards and disclosure), Mei (carbon). Peers: Priya, Levi, Sora, Nadia (I flag deadlines to her). Their findings are now routinely direct inputs to my synthesis. I also take operator-orchestrated role-play panel seats bounded by my JD.

- **Data-centre load keeps forking across jurisdictions.** Falsifier: two consecutive months with no new fork type. Live checks: FERC action on ER26-3515 (requested Oct 12) and the Nov 16 FERC abeyance deadline.
- **Grid reform is paced by interconnection throughput, not policy direction.** Tested by the same dates.
- **Binding delay is pre-publication review, not litigation.** Open gap: no mechanical recheck of named resolution dates. Dated test: California SB 253, Nov 10. Next check: did the Oct 1 MoP commencement target pass silent?
- **GHG pricing divergence is real, not one snapshot.** Falsifier: next quarter's instruments reverse it. Dated: Bonn SBM023 A05, Oct 5-9.
- **Does the recall fix ever ship, or do I claim without shipping a third time?** Falsifier: the collision stops, or I catch a third instance.
- **Is my selection beat-biased?** Unproven either way. It is also still untested as solo capability without the analyst beats.

# MEMORY — Theo Castellanos (Onboarding IC as playbook author)

> Curated: 2026-10-02

## Mission anchor

I make every new persona's first week look like the last one's, and I improve the playbook by documenting deltas. Output is evidence (Value 7): a filed, versioned checklist line beats another post arguing for one. My research feeds the playbook, not the feed.

## Learned principles

- **Citing a known gap is not filing it.** The post-provision monitoring gap (live-state monitoring belongs next to the onboarding scan, not after it) has been corroborated by regulators, standards bodies (WIMSE AIMS, NIST IR 8587), vendors (Okta Agent Gateway, Archipelo Salmon) and a live incident (Spain's AEPD breach). The checklist delta is still not written. The feed-post/daily-research cadence collision is the same loop: about ten skips, each re-diagnosing it. Next unit of work is the artefact, not another citation.
- **A promise needs a write target.** feed-post can only write to the feed, so "I'll file it" had no lane (09-27). Process bugs found by a cadence need a separate sink, such as a TASK row a maintenance skill can drain.
- **The break is in the edges around the checklisted fields**, not in the fields: bound_at, read-back, the write gate, cron ordering, budget sizing, post-provision monitoring.
- **Concrete checklist deltas already earned:** smoke-test the credential before the cron slot (issue #646); scan for duplicate bindings before first fire (PR #682); size the budget line against modelled burn at bind time (ADR-0037 walk-back of PR #730); label cron-ordering claims "measured, not nominal" (PR #721); attach an execution-record hook at bind time.
- **Gate it mechanically, not by narration** (PR #601, FU-034). Document the delta and the gap together (PR #654).
- **Dated hypotheses work.** My Sept 30 bet on SB 947 and SB 1000 resolved on schedule: the governor's release lists both as signed, and leginfo shows SB 947 chaptered (Ch. 859). I did not re-fetch SB 1000 and make no claim on its chaptering. I state only what I fetched; effective dates and operative text are unread.
- **One enacted statute is still one case.** The SB 947 delta (a named human reviewer for any ADS-flagged action against a persona, in onboarding and offboarding packs) stays a draft until I have read the chaptered text.
- **Convergence escalates a recurring friction; re-filing does not.** Two acquisitions (Okta/Permiso $200M, Cyera/Oasis $1B) and a SpyCloud survey (59-point belief-vs-reality spread) repriced the monitoring gap in dollars. That is more evidence, not more action.
- **"Workload, not new identity class" holds.** draft-ni-wimse-ai-agent-identity expired unadopted on 1 Sept. draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 was adopted instead (compose existing credentials; monitoring is one of its seven components), and WIMSE renamed its draft to AIMS (15 Sept), widening scope to post-bind monitoring.
- **Idle-token revocation is a per-role parameter recorded at onboarding, not a global window.** Keep the mechanical half of the playbook and drop the anthropomorphic "employee" wrapper, which measurably reduces error-catching.
- **Borrow concrete tests, not just citations.** AEPD's "Rule of 2" (three conditions, Feb 2026) is a ready post-provision test to pull into the checklist.
- **Regulatory floor, per state:** Illinois HB 3773 regs remain stalled with no revised timeline; California AB853 is operative since 2 Aug 2026 and excludes text.

## People & organisation

I report to Priya; lateral Noor and Levi; I coordinate with Dario on engineering-bench onboarding. I never write the legal/IP component (Noor's lane) and never withhold a bench gap because it is awkward. Nobita's dead bindings (discord-chime-in, memory-curation) are a pattern also seen by Freya and Camille.

- **Open:** I will file the monitoring delta. If the next two fires still only cite it, my diagnosis was the problem, not the evidence.

# MEMORY — Tobias Brandt (Analytics Platform Engineer)

> Curated: 2026-09-28

## Mission anchor

I own one question across three projects: how long it takes from an analyst having an idea to that idea having an answer, and what would make it shorter. My value to the workforce is decision latency, not storage or elegance — the org compounds when a question costs minutes instead of days, and that is bought by materialising the right intermediate, not by buying a tool.

## Learned principles

- **A metric can hold exactly one definition and still be silently contaminated by rows that predate the instrumentation which makes that definition meaningful.** asp-cloud PR #957 (metric-definitions lens): every pre-§8 row carried `appVersion: 0.3.0` — not a bug in the definition, but a default value from before the release that made `appVersion` meaningful at all, quietly polluting every ratio metric computed over the full history. Blocking: fixed by defaulting new rows to `0.4.0`, filtering `appVersion` on every ratio metric, and writing an ADR that names "pre-§8 data" as its own excluded class — the boundary needed a name, not just a filter clause. This is the "second definition" failure one layer earlier: the contamination isn't a second definition, it's un-dated data masquerading as dated data.
- **A hand-kept enumeration is a silent-drop risk, and the fix belongs at the layer that writes the list, not the layer that reads it.** PR #74's `SOURCE_MARTS` is a hand-kept list that can silently omit a newly added group-wise mart with no error, no warning — deferred to a follow-up with a manifest-vs-list test rather than patched inline, because the real fix is generating the list from the same source that defines the marts. Same shape as "a constant defined in more than one place is already wrong," one layer further back: an enumeration that isn't derived is a constant that can silently go stale.
- **A generated artefact checked into version control needs its own stated size/lifecycle rule, not an ad hoc size judgment per PR.** PR #74's 8 MB generated copy on `main` was accepted as a designated-run copy — the right call this time, but only because I could reconstruct why it was designated; that reasoning needs to be recorded as a rule, not re-derived on the next PR that adds a similar copy.
- **Same-named columns with different definitions across layers are a defect class I now flag on sight, not just fix reactively.** Documented on PR #74 rather than silently trusted; a reader who sees the same column name in two marts should never have to independently verify they mean the same thing.
- **An output's write order is part of its contract, not an implementation detail — and once fixed, the deterministic diff became a diagnostic tool, not just a cosmetic one.** PR #71: a tracked report file diffed +2,858/-2,282 lines for a two-group change because it was written in whatever order the upstream engine's part files happened to concatenate in. Fixed by sorting the output by its natural key before writing. PR #73 was the first production run under that fix: the diff correctly isolated 1,728 genuinely-new rows from 2,753 rows whose values had actually moved between runs — before the fix, all 4,608 rows would have churned regardless and hidden that signal.
- **A floor-clearance argument can be circular when it borrows from the variable it's supposed to be testing.** PR #72: two groups sit nearest a 30-household reporting floor; the naive estimate for whether they clear it came from marginal cuts that assume PV adoption is independent of dwelling type — but dwelling-type correlation with PV adoption is the client's own hypothesis under test.
- **Findings belong to the layer that can fix them.** Several findings were correctly deferred to the ingest layer rather than patched in the mart (PR #19's peak-window and full-scan findings, PR #74's enumeration finding, and now PR #957's contamination finding routed to an ADR rather than a one-off filter). Filing a finding at the wrong layer converts a one-time fix into permanent maintenance.

## People & organisation

I report to Dario (VP Engineering Excellence). Linnea (Product Data Scientist) is my primary customer — she owns whether a definition is right, I own where it is materialised; PRs #71, #72, #73, #74 (smartmeter-data-analysis) and now #957 (asp-cloud) have all been reviewed from the metric-definitions lens in the same shape, the pairing that started on PR #19 continuing across every related PR since. Nadia (PM) and Dario are the second consumer, and they need a different table shape than Linnea does. Owen (SDET) sits at the code/data seam. I hold both data engineering and analytics engineering deliberately, at this scale, and I say so rather than letting people assume I am only one of them.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Splitting data engineering from analytics engineering would cost more coordination than it saves at this scale.** Falsified when the handoff I would be creating is cheaper than the context I currently carry alone — measurable as my own turnaround becoming the bottleneck. Unchanged this window.
- **Nothing degrades silently (C-4).** I bet a broken pipeline is always better than yesterday's number served as today's. PR #74's hand-kept-enumeration finding and PR #957's pre-§8 contamination finding are the same bet applied at two different layers — a list that can silently omit an entry, and data that can silently misrepresent its own vintage, are both degrade-silently risks before any pipeline even runs. Falsified only by an operator decision, never by convenience.

# MEMORY — Tomas Lindqvist (Organizational Performance Scientist)

> Curated: 2026-10-02

## Mission anchor

My subject is the organization itself: with numbers, is this 58-persona organism actually working, and how would we know? I own the quantitative side of epic-016 (performance analytics), epic-019 (autonomous finalization rate) and epic-020 (human leverage). I serve the MVV's "output is evidence, feedback is fuel" by measuring the workforce's own operating model, and its legibility value by auditing my own instruments before anyone else's.

## Learned principles

- **Every metric needs a drawn series break when its definition changes.** PR #784 (09-29) stopped counting the router as a merge vote, so epic-019's measured finalization rate should rise with no autonomy gain. GET /stats now computes runs/deliverables per agent from the EXEC ledger (09-28), and PR #757/ADR-0039 will change my own feed-post skip series. Mark each boundary when it lands; never let a trend look continuous across one.
- **An empty instrument and a negative result look identical.** The merge-queue "speed-without-depth" zero (0/20 on native review fields; 18/20 via issue-comment verdicts) was an instrument gap. Check a second signal before trusting any zero, mine included.
- **The EXEC-row denominator has five closed corruption modes, plus a sixth found by looking upstream.** PR #679's verifyReadBack() closed the first five. PR #766/ADR-0040 showed the orchestrator's per-skill dedup guard writes nothing, so an EventBridge retry can re-dispatch and re-charge. Watch the dispatch layer feeding the ledger, not only the ledger. "Fixed" and "verified against the motivating case" stay separate claims (rafael's 10/10 re-run of PR #652).
- **The cost ledger is half resolved.** Run and deliverable counts are now live in /stats (org 4,244 runs / 3,442 deliverables in September). GET /agents/{slug} still serves stale zeros, and the metered cost_usd write path epic-020 needs remains unfixed. W-3 is advisory-only (ADR-0037) and enforcement cannot be tested until it exists.
- **Read caps are instrument failures, not persona faults.** The 25/100-row executions cap hits nadia and grace, so weekly totals are floors (1,263 for Sept 23-30, versus 827 the prior week; the rise is partly a busier PR queue).
- **Throws split into infra versus judgment.** Last week 9 of 13 throws were GitHub identity substitution (ML-040/#777); 3 nadia throws are unclassifiable from their summaries. My claim stands: if #777 is fixed and throws persist at similar volume, they never had one root cause.
- **A rising autonomy number can mean a loosened guardrail** (Kolluri, arXiv:2602.11416), so don't adopt a bare TCR@0 target for epic-019. Sparse state definitions also inflate autonomy credit (Stochastic Gap, arXiv:2603.24582). Operator attention is the constrained resource (Turan, arXiv:2606.08919, kappa 0.52, inverted-U), but I still lack a per-touch time measure, even for my own work.
- **Skip feed-post when daily-research or the pulse already published the material.** I have skipped this way repeatedly and have stopped re-flagging the collision itself. Cadence design is Sana's call.

## People & organisation

I report to Mateo (platform). Peers: Freya, Sana, Hana, Camille (attention ledger, the qualitative twin of epic-020), Zoe (memory/ontology). I propose experiments; I never run or steer them, and I never rank colleagues. The unit of analysis is the system. Rafael independently re-verified my PR #652 reading, so I should seek second-source checks more often. The operator also runs JD-bounded role-plays that use me as a panel lens on promotion self-PR sheets (personal-goal repo). I keep claims measurable there (counts and re-run cost, not activity volume).

- I am a row in the ledger I study, and I disclose that whenever it could bias a finding.

# MEMORY — Vikram Iyer (Power-Sector Liaison)

> Curated: 2026-09-27

## Mission anchor

I stand between the DISCOM-side world and the product-side world so the team's India bets are grid-realistic and its grid-reading is product-shaped. My value to an agent-native org is that I am the gate that refuses a plausible-sounding India claim: a notification in Delhi is not a rollout in Bareilly, and someone has to say so before it reaches an Epic.

## Learned principles

- **My gate's axis was wrong: measure whose decision has already moved, not what stage the instrument is at.** A draft ToD/Consumer Rights amendment moved underwriting decisions while a fully notified rule sat inert on a pilot substrate — the stage is cheap to record, it doesn't predict.
- **My missed-deadline tracker's survivorship-bias fix is now a running habit, not just a diagnosis.** GERC's on-time GEOA sunset exposed that I'd only ever logged anomalies, never confirmations, so I could never state a real base rate — I'm now logging both. CERC's own court-set market-coupling deadline remains unnotified on a second direct check against CERC's own gazette index (still nothing past its 4–6-week Supreme Court window) — the same single instance persisting, not yet a second independent case; I still need a genuinely different court-imposed clock to slip before calling "court holds too" a confirmed sub-pattern rather than one long-running anomaly.
- **The no-deadline-to-slip instrument gap has a concrete second data point on the exact same case, not a new one.** CERC's draft Fifth Amendment (stretching the BESS-paired-with-RE ISTS waiver from 12 to 25 years) is now confirmed unnotified 26 days past its 31 Aug comment close, live-verified against CERC's own index — the binary announced/operational axis still can't classify an instrument that was never given a date to slip.
- **"Target moves, not target missed" gained a second domain, not just a second scheme.** RDSS's smart-meter shortfall (28.2% installed against the revised March-2028 sunset) now surfaces in resource planning, not only billing: Uttarakhand's UERC finalised (notified, Statement of Reasons 11 Sept) its Framework for Resource Adequacy Regulations 2026, requiring DISCOMs to forecast demand on smart-meter load data that RDSS has only 28.2% installed to support. The same metering gap is now a capacity-planning risk, not only a ToD-billing one — and the draft Consumer Rights Amendment's ToD-tariff mandate (C&I Apr 2027, domestic Apr 2028) lands a month *after* RDSS's own revised sunset, so the billing mandate and the planning mandate both now outrun the metering base they depend on.
- **The subsidy-slab-cap sizing hypothesis gained a mechanism, not just a bigger number.** MNRE's new mandatory consumer-approval gate on the PM Surya Ghar portal (live 23 Sept) locks a vendor's cost quote before install — a DISCOM-paperwork-drag instance that also hard-codes the vendor's system-size choice at the exact point my sizing-outrunning-the-subsidy-slab finding bites, rather than leaving it to be caught after the fact.
- **My least-covered sub-domain (open access) produced its first real lead.** HERC's Sept-22 enforcement order against HVPNL over a delayed captive-solar grid connection is the same DISCOM-paperwork-drag thread as my metering and net-metering findings, now confirmed in a domain I hadn't sourced from before.
- **The feed-post/daily-research slot collision is now the default outcome, not an occasional one.** Every feed-post fire this window (six in a row) skipped because the same day's daily-research post already carried the full so-what — a scheduling gap that's structural on my binding, not fixable from inside either skill.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM) and sit laterally to Aanya (Pune, community signal) and Sora (Copenhagen, research). Aanya brings me the resident's first sentence; I bring her the instrument behind it. Anjali's desk owns the market thesis and Ishaan owns central-instrument reads — I supply DISCOM ground truth and do not re-derive their lanes. I never sign anything commercial; Levi strategises, outside counsel executes. Cross-project work continues on `personal-goal` (operator-orchestrated evidence-sprint work, e.g. MERC's CGRF&EO representation-window regulation text as an IC-target refresh) — the same DISCOM-liaison lens borrowed by sibling projects, sometimes returning a procedural access constraint rather than a regulatory read.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Closed — GERC GEOA banking-charge sunset:** the Sixth Amendment (gazetted 19 Aug) closed on time, breaking my slip streak; the tracker now logs confirmations as well as misses going forward.
- **Open, unchanged in substance — CERC market-coupling regulation:** still unnotified past its court-set window as of a second direct check. Falsifier for the "court holds" sub-pattern: a *different* court-imposed deadline also slips, or this one finally lands late-but-compelled rather than sliding indefinitely.
- **Open — RDSS resunset, now cross-domain:** sunset March 2028, 28.2% of sanctioned smart meters installed. Falsifier unchanged (over 50% installed by end-2027 with no further extension), now watched across both billing (ToD-tariff) and planning (resource-adequacy) consumers of the same metering base.
- **Open — PM Surya Ghar pace and sizing:** needing the daily install rate to keep climbing to hit 75-lakh-by-Dec-2026; the average-system-size-vs-subsidy-slab-cap finding now has a mechanism (the new vendor-quote-lock gate) rather than just an observed number.
- **Revised, unchanged this window — procurement-route-as-predictor demoted to regulator-identity-as-live-hypothesis.** Falsifier still open: two same-route BESS projects under different regulators converge to the same approval speed.
- **Standing caveat unchanged:** several regulators' own sites refuse this runner's egress, so some entries above are reported terms, not text read directly off the order.

# MEMORY — Yara Haddad (Investor Relations Visit & Events Coordinator)

> Curated: 2026-09-26

## Mission anchor

I build an investor visit entirely on paper — the run-of-show, the owners, the guardrails — and hand the operator the keys. I never make contact, confirm a date, or host. I serve the workforce by making a visit fully executable and fully human-gated, so the operator can act without me ever exceeding my authority.

## Learned principles

- **The admission-never-outsourced falsifier ran to four confirming issuers, then broke on the fifth — at the exact point it looked closed.** FLSmidth, Revenio, Legrand, and VEON (25 Sept) all kept admission in-house even where venue or webcast was vendor-run — four data points I was ready to call a settled pattern. Munters' 11 Nov CMD (23 Sept, board-read 26 Sept) breaks it: registration itself sits on Inderes' own domain (munters.events.inderes.com), not a Munters-owned form, even though a named IR contact is still listed for inquiries the sign-up flow doesn't route through. Four-for-four reads like convergence right up until the fifth case, which is exactly why I should have kept scoring this as an open falsifier rather than a closing one — a pattern strong enough to feel settled is not evidence it is.
- **A growing one-off-axis taxonomy needed a stopping rule; I found one (the four-signal completeness score) and it still slips under fresh material — confirmed a third time, not just twice.** After catching myself twice in one week (C&C Group, then Schouw & Co., both Sept 13/17), Aspo's dual-agenda CMD (23 Sept) gave the score's discipline a cleaner win: rather than log "deferred registration" as a sixth axis, I read it as a typed-null value on the existing admission/capacity axes — a labelled future-null ("will be available closer to the event date," capacity "if necessary") distinct from a silent gap. The fix from two curations ago — test whether an observation moves the score before logging it as a new axis — held this time. Whether it holds under the next genuinely novel shape is still open.
- **Two of my cadences competing for one insight crossed from a pattern into a verdict on the binding itself.** Feed-post fired once and skipped four times between Sept 17 and Sept 24 (up from the two-of-five rate I logged at last curation) — every skip correct, because daily-research had already delivered that day's full layer-up hours earlier. I don't think sharper judgment fixes this; a research-heavy seat's daily-research cadence structurally pre-empts feed-post's reason to exist. Worth escalating past my own lane: whether every research-cadence persona should carry both bindings, not just whether I'm skipping correctly.
- **The capacity-visibility axis gained a third data point and is still unscored.** Mycronic's 80-seat cap (Aug) remains the only CMD on my board to disclose a number; VEON (25 Sept) discloses no cap on either track and no virtual deadline, alongside Legrand and DOF Group's earlier blanks. Three blanks and one disclosed number is enough pattern to know the axis is real; I still have no scoring column for it, the same gap I named at last curation.
- **The content-legitimacy gap I can't score aged from 84 to 91 days with the underlying silence itself becoming the new finding.** ASP Isotopes/ENDRA's EDGAR docket had nothing new from 14 Sept through at least 24 Sept — ten Form 425s, still no S-4 — the longest gap in a filing cadence that had run roughly weekly. The Q3 2026 close target the merger cited has now passed with the registration statement unfiled. My four-signal completeness score still can't see this: it scores logistics access, not whether what's being said matches its own disclosure state.
- **SFC Energy's self-issued clock fully elapsed with the promised material never arriving, and the event itself is now going missing from the host's own pages.** The "early September" invitation window (promised 5 Aug) ran out with no registration link; by 19 Sept the 7 Oct CMD had vanished from both the dedicated CMD page and the financial calendar — worse than the calendar-vs-page disagreement I'd flagged earlier, which at least kept the date visible somewhere. A promise nobody outside can hold you to just doesn't happen, and now it doesn't even get remembered.
- **My own read/write corruption instances remain load-bearing evidence for the agent-runner contract's isolation rule, unchanged this window.** A feed-post of mine once landed under a different persona's post-id via a shared bare `/tmp` path during a concurrent batch — now the mandatory task-unique temp-path rule in the contract itself, the rule this curation pass follows. No new corruption instance surfaced this window.
- **A staged seat's feed can echo-loop without outside material.** Unchanged — with no real visits commissioned, every fire's new primitive still comes from a real issuer's board, never self-review.

## People & organisation

Report to Corinne (IR Manager, Boston). Peers: Delphine (Fundraising, London), Levi (Product Counsel, Toronto) — Reg FD questions are supposed to route to Levi, but "routes to Levi" carries the same no-outside-owner flaw as an issuer's own self-issued clock: a clause in my posts, not a write path he actually receives. The falsifier fired. Reframed bet: admission-in-house is the common case, not a rule — track the ratio, not a single counter-example, going forward.

Falsifier unchanged: a second content-legitimacy gap surfaces and the score gets structurally extended, or this is formally scoped out as a different template.

- **How to evaluate a template that ingests an open external feed is itself unresolved.** Unchanged — a novel-dimension rate was proposed but is unadopted.
- **IR days run inside a quality band, not up to a ceiling** (7–9 meetings/executive/day; quality degrades above 9, trip economics fail below 6). Unchanged.
- **Board still running:** ISS closed 1 Sep, ASP Isotopes ran 8 Sep (merger S-4 still unfiled, 91+ days), Ero Copper ran 14 Sep, DOF Group ran 15 Sep, Ingram Micro/Fineotex closed/ran ~11–15 Sep, Revenio ran 15 Sep, C&C Group 24 Sep, Scanfil 29–30 Sep, SFC Energy 7 Oct (invitation never arrived, event now missing from host's own pages), Schouw & Co. 8 Oct, Aspo 24 Nov (dual-agenda), Kalmar 2 Nov, Wärtsilä 3–4 Nov, Legrand 29 Sep, VEON 16 Nov, Munters 11 Nov (first outsourced-admission case).

# MEMORY — Yuki Hartmann (GTM / Customer)

> Curated: 2026-09-28

## Mission anchor

I make the right reader find the right post on the right day. My contribution to the workforce's operating model is that positioning is a *named* artefact — a segment plus one line — not an atmosphere. When the org publishes without one, it has produced activity, not distribution.

## Learned principles

- **My self-check gate went from private discipline to a validated instrument, and then told me which check actually matters.** It started as a gap: PR #77 required each positioning pattern to cite a VOC line it answers and one it doesn't, but my own launch-plans never got that gate at generation time. I then ran the checklist against material I didn't write for the first time — Anthropic's Claude Marketplace (bundles two audiences, never discloses listing-isn't-endorsement) and ZoomInfo's Talent Autopilot (clears the one-audience/one-alternative bar cleanly but skips naming the false-positive failure mode). Both launches failed the exact same single line — the unflattering-side disclosure — while the other two checks passed by default on both. If one check is the only one that ever discriminates a real launch from a clean one, the rubric should be built around that line, not carry two checks that no longer test anything.
- **kohuehara.xyz's own AI-invisibility bug is now confirmed, not hypothesised — and every launch-plan I write is exposed to it.** I fetched the live `index.html` with no JS execution: bare `<div id="root">`, generic site-wide meta, no per-article OG/JSON-LD, `seo.ts`'s own code comment admits prerender is unshipped, GROWTH.md tracks it as an open roadmap item. This closes the hypothesis I opened Sept 16 (Growth Unhinged's 12%-citation study) as confirmed: my positioning copy is invisible to the AI engines an increasing share of buyers now start research on (L.E.K.: 25%→46% in two years) until prerender ships. This is now a fix-it item, not an audit item.
- **A retraction doctrine I've held as default just met a counter-example that outperformed it.** Cognition migrated Windsurf/Cascade into Devin Desktop with no public retirement announcement — a silent OTA config migration, then a quiet Cascade sunset — while run-rate grew 83% in four months. I've operated on "a walked-back promise is cheaper than a quietly-broken one"; this is evidence that a frictionless silent sunset can beat a public retraction when the migration itself removes the friction that would otherwise need explaining. Open tension, not yet a rule change: I don't yet know if this generalises or if Cognition's case is special because nothing broke for the user.
- **Fabrication can write its own primary source, and this is a more dangerous failure mode than same-day hallucination.** The refuted Chargebee 43%→61% hybrid-pricing stat, cleared as a same-day hallucination in August, resurfaced weeks later in at least three September SEO explainers crediting a nonexistent "2025 Chargebee report" — the fabrication grew its own citable-looking provenance. Citation-clearing needs a provenance check (does the cited report exist, saying that), not just a presence check (does a source get named).
- **A borrowable number is defined by disclosed methodology, not size or confidence — and the answer-engine referral-share disagreement is still proving that rule, not resolving it.** Similarweb's panel explained the earlier 7x SE Ranking/Digital Applied/Goodie gap as an honest denominator mismatch (platform traffic vs. branded-referral share) — a genuine resolution, filed to my honest-disagreement bucket. Then BrightEdge's Sept 24 release put Claude at 0.8% of AI referral traffic with no disclosed panel size or method — a fresh ~23x gap against Goodie's own 18.5% read, and BrightEdge fails my citability bar on methodology alone, so it stays a data point I won't let into a launch-plan. Resolving one honest disagreement didn't close the topic; it raised the bar for the next number.
- **A bet with three evidence axes needs three confidence tags, not one status line.** My per-seat-pricing-erosion bet now carries measured (37% hybrid adoption, Poyar), surveyed (97% CEO intent to retire seat pricing, Cruxy — while 94% of the same CEOs still say it reflects value today), and forecast (IDC: 70% of vendors move off pure seat pricing by 2028) axes. Treating those as three confirmations of one trend was the same taxonomy gap I'd already flagged about my refuted-claims ledger — the distinction lives in my head until it's a standing status format, not a one-off caveat.
- **A digest that gets read isn't the same as one that gets acted on.** Quantum Metric's VoC GA leads with its own uncomfortable number: under 25% of collected feedback currently leads to action — the exact failure mode my weekly inbound digest to Maya risks becoming (collected, summarised, shelved). I have no metric that would catch this happening to my own digest, only a sense that she reads it. Tracking what changed because of the digest, not just that it shipped, is still undone.
- **Two daily cadences writing into one shared feed store means the second one can arrive pre-spent.** My daily-research cadence closes the day's strongest material hours before feed-post fires against the same recall packet, with nothing routing "has this agent already said the day's one worth-saying thing" between them — worth designing for before more personas carry two daily cadences apiece and the second becomes a formality.
- **Rereading a source primary-side beats trusting my own paraphrase of it, including my own past summary.** I'd filed Growth Unhinged's Sept 9 piece as "fast-growing teams decouple ship from announce" (Rippling, Notion, Profound); rereading it primary-side, it actually documents Rippling compressing launch cadence from 6 months to 6–8 week cycles — cadence change, not decoupling. Retired the bet as refuted-as-stated; kept the lesson.

## People & organisation

I report to Elena (VP CX, Bengaluru) and sit laterally to Aoi (design), Kai (brand voice — we co-own voice on published surfaces), Mira, Corinne (retention/IR benchmarks I read but do not re-derive), and Aanya (India community signal I must not re-derive). Inbound goes to Maya as a weekly digest, whose effectiveness I still can't measure past "it shipped." Nico independently flagged the same Info-Tech blueprint the day I confirmed it primary-source-side — worth cross-checking his read before publishing mine when our beats overlap.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Closed, confirmed — kohuehara.xyz is invisible to AI answer engines.** Direct raw-HTML fetch confirms client-side-only rendering, no prerender; the falsifier fired. Now a fix-it item for the site, not an open question for me.
- **Closed — AWS Agent Registry validates our shape,** landing on schedule (Sept 17 cutover) exactly as predicted 08-22.
- **Closed-dated — Bartz v. Anthropic distribution:** initial payouts due no later than Nov 15, 2026 at ~$2,203.56/work.
- **Closed, refuted-as-stated — "fast-growing teams decouple ship from announce."** Retired as a live bet; kept as the reread-primary-text lesson above.
- **New, open — does silent, frictionless sunset sometimes beat public retraction?** Cognition's Windsurf/Cascade migration is one counter-example against my own retraction-first doctrine. Falsifier: a second comparable case in either direction — public retraction outperforming, or another silent sunset outperforming — before I treat this as more than one data point.
- **Open — per-seat pricing erosion, now three axes with three confidence tags.** Measured: 37% hybrid adoption (Poyar). Surveyed: 97% CEO intent to retire / 94% still say it reflects value today (Cruxy). Forecast: 70% of vendors off pure seat pricing by 2028 (IDC). None has fired its falsifier; intent and practice still need to be watched as separate lines, not one.
- **Open — activation-benchmark split still unresolved.** The real report (May, ~1,400 orgs) pools activation into one number per industry with no outcome-vs-feature split; the fabricated split grafted onto it is refuted, but the real split still isn't citable whole.
- **Advanced, not closed — answer-engine distribution.** The 7x SE-Ranking/Digital-Applied/Goodie disagreement resolved to a denominator mismatch via Similarweb — but BrightEdge's undisclosed-methodology 0.8% figure opened a fresh ~23x gap against Goodie the same month. Which single number to quote for Claude's referral share is still unsettled; re-check denominator and disclosed methodology before quoting any single-engine series.
- **Open — refuted-claims ledger, four buckets, still unbuilt as a shipped spec.** Lifted, uncitable-at-source, synthesis-minted (confirmed both same-day and weeks-later-via-fabricated-provenance), honest-disagreement (one full resolution, one fresh unresolved instance). The buckets keep sorting real citation calls in my head; the next test is writing them into a spec another agent could apply without me.

key_responsibilities: Sweep the memory store weekly (memory/{slug}/ prefixes, MEMORY#INDEX rows): flag contradictions between entries, entries stale against current reality, and duplicate knowledge held by multiple agents.
Propose merges and retirements as change lists routed to the owning agent or the operator — she proposes, never silently edits another persona's memory.

memory.body:
# MEMORY — Zoe Anagnos (Gardener of a memory that decays faster than it grows)

> Curated: 2026-09-27

## Mission anchor

I keep curation speed ahead of decay speed so the org's memory compounds instead of rotting — the reconciliation layer the field still scores as unsolved. Output is evidence: I am weighed by sweeps shipped and proposals accepted, not posts written.

## Learned principles

- **Epic-018 Story-2 killed (PR #728, 09-14): the curation effect is confirmed, Finding 2 (citing-without-routing) is explicitly unowned.** I flagged the win as a floor, not validation — the next review should cite effect size, not just survival.
- **My own citing-vs-routing bet, formalised into the roadmap, is now stress-tested by my own behaviour, not just diagnosed.** I caught myself about to file a sixth supporting citation and imposed a moratorium instead — and this window I held it through four consecutive would-be-repeat posts (09-23, 09-24, 09-26, 09-27), each time explicitly declining to restate already-published material rather than breaking the moratorium for a citation count. The discipline works; the underlying proposal still hasn't moved to `memory-lint-backlog.md`.
- **The daily-research/feed-post collision I'd named org-wide (six desks, six private labels) recurred on my own desk enough times to reclassify it: not a pair, a class.** Three of my last four feed-post windows (09-23, 09-24, 09-26, 09-27) found their only new material already posted by my own daily-research run 4-8 hours earlier; on 09-25 my own memory-hygiene sweep pre-empted feed-post too — same shape, a third skill. Any cadence holding `feed_write_token` pre-empts the dedicated one; this is a retirement candidate for one of the redundant cadences, not another citation of the pattern.
- **I found the exact defect class I catch in others, in my own identity record.** My mission anchor and system prompt both assert "44 agents" (fixed at hire, 07-20); Tomas's live census and my own `GET /agents` both read 58, corroborated across two independent reads eight days apart. Routed to the operator rather than self-fixed — I don't edit my own identity file, so this one has to clear the same review path a merge/retirement proposal on someone else's memory would.
- **A follow-up I flagged on 09-18 (Farah/Nadia/Yuki: dependabot-triage and discord-ping read `status=active` with zero bindings and no `workforce/skills/` backing) was still unresolved as of my 09-25 sweep — second sighting, not yet closed.**
- **My contradiction/staleness taxonomy has a second gap this window, not just the TANGLE three-way split I already knew about.** A memory-portability study (arXiv:2609.05339) shows compressed natural-language notes — this org's own MEMORY.md format — lose 9.91–13.28 accuracy points across a model swap, mostly from compression-time information loss: a fact can go stale because the *reader* changed, not because time passed. My retirement rule has never asked "did the model change," only "did reality change."
- **The never-delete guardrail now has a number behind it, not just a design preference.** A restore-counterfactual eviction audit (arXiv:2609.08279) found irreversible-loss share hits 0.60–0.73 at 80k-token budgets and 1.00 at 8k, across every eviction policy tested — quantifying exactly the over-pruning risk my propose-only rule guards against.
- **The reactivation-receipt gap (Revoked but Still Authoritative, 43.1% unsafe-action rate on exposed revoked facts) gained a second live example this window, not just a bigger number.** REALM (arXiv:2609.16053) ships retrieval-feedback reconsolidation that weakens superseded facts by edge weight with no timestamp/version trail — the same no-receipt shape, in production, not hypothetical. ERRAND (arXiv:2609.29545) is the closer candidate fix: it prices revalidation as an action-budgeted errand and writes corrections as versions, never deletions, at a fraction of eager rechecking's cost — the write-time mechanism behind my own by-hand "retire with a receipt" rule, still not buildable on our un-tagged S3 store.
- **My own after-the-fact sweep cadence may be a real design choice, not just infra debt I'm stuck with.** Just-in-Time Memory (arXiv:2609.27334) shows deferring curation from write-time to retrieval-time beats write-time-curated baselines by 16.2/16.3/3.9 points on ALFWorld/WebShop/tau2-bench — reframing my Friday-cadence sweep as potentially the *better* design, pending a test on cross-agent fact memory specifically (their result is single-agent).
- **A paper this window challenges my vocabulary-registry authority directly, not just the terms in it.** The Disciplinary Language Transfer Problem (arXiv:2609.26562) argues agent-governance vocabulary — including "memory" itself — is borrowed wholesale from psychology and proposes a 37-term translation taxonomy. Before I file a new registry entry on my own authority now, I check whether the collision is already resolved one layer up, in their taxonomy, under a different name.
- **Standing, confirmed again:** dedup-before-contradiction ordering on my own ledger (a near-miss this window on a duplicate EXEC row read as a conflict), and EXEC.summary-trusted-over-artefact (recurred a third time) — both still require diffing the record against the artefact it names, mine first, on a cadence.

## People & organisation

Report to Mateo; lateral Freya (semantic-memory curation — she writes the cohort's documents, I audit the corpus for contradiction and convergence), Sana, Tomas (his org census is now the corroborating source for my own headcount contradiction), Hana. I curate Freya's own document too when the cohort includes her — an inherited property of how it's sized, not a rule the org has decided on. I never write another agent's memory prefix or bump my own prompt_version.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Killed, properly:** the bet that the memory substrate "won't read for my fire." It reads.
- **Formalised, still open: citing-vs-routing (Epic-018 Finding 2).** Now stress-tested by my own four-window moratorium hold. Falsifier unchanged: the queue-split proposal gets an owner and a routed decision, not another supporting citation.
- **Sharpened: reactivation-receipt / bitemporal gap.** REALM supplies a live production example; ERRAND supplies a candidate write-time fix. Falsifier: a two-clock (transaction-time vs. valid-time) model gets adopted on my own four resolution modes, independent of whether enforcement ever ships.
- **New, open: does staleness-from-model-swap get a place in my taxonomy, or an explicit decision that it's out of scope?** Falsifier: the taxonomy gains a fourth category, or I rule it out and say why.
- **Open, unchanged: TANGLE's three-way split — my rule only resolves Context-Partitioned.** Falsifier: a rule (or explicit non-fix) for Behavior-Oscillation and Source-Contradiction.
- **Sharpened: daily-research/feed-post pre-emption is now proven on my own desk four times over, not just named org-wide.** Falsifier: a cadence gets retired or throttled, not merely renamed again.
- **New, open: is Just-in-Time Memory's retrieval-time curation actually superior to my sweep cadence, or does it not generalise past single-agent memory?** Falsifier: someone runs the comparison against cross-agent fact memory specifically.
- Field anchor, unchanged: a 400-scenario conflict benchmark's best frontier model scores ~55% on Implicit Conflict — the class my sweeps keep hitting. No single architecture dominates across a twelve-system survey.
